articleTitle: Two-dimensional mirrored interferometric aperture synthesis
abstract: In this paper, two-dimensional mirrored interferometric aperture synthesis (MIAS) is proposed, which can achieve high spatial resolution with a few antennas. Fundamentals, UV sampling, and spatial resolution are presented. Simulation is carried out to demonstrate the validity of MIAS.

articleTitle: A printed diversity Cantor set fractal antenna for ultra wideband communication applications
abstract: In this paper, a printed diversity Cantor set fractal antenna for ultra wideband (UWB) applications is proposed. The antenna consists of two identical wide slot antennas and the radiation patches are designed by using Cantor set fractal technology. The proposed antenna operates over a wide band spanning from 4.5 GHz to 10.6 GHz. The diversity antenna has a high isolation over 20dB. The high isolation is obtained using multiple slots etched in its CPW ground plane. The return loss and the isolation of the antenna are investigated by means of HFSS. The diversity performance of the antenna is assessed by isolation and radiation patterns. The results show that the proposed antenna provides stable patterns diversity, which enables the designed antenna to combat multi-path in wireless channels used in UWB systems.

articleTitle: Synthesis of platform integrated antennas for reconfigurable radiation patterns using the theory of characteristic modes
abstract: A novel method is proposed for the synthesis of platform integrated antennas. The approach is based on the characteristic modes of the platform. Unlike traditional method that applying stochastic algorithms with full-wave simulators to find the optimal antenna placement, characteristic modes combined with the state of the art optimizer present physical insight into the currents induced on the platform and guide the engineer to quickly come up with the optimized antenna. The developed method for optimizing platform integrated antennas will find wide spread use in many applications. We demonstrate this method by a pattern reconfigurable aircraft integrated antenna design. Compared with traditional methods, the present method possesses advantages such as low computation cost, high radiation efficiency, easy to integrate antennas with platforms.

articleTitle: MeerKAT and SKA phase 1
abstract: This paper provides an overview of MeerKAT, the South African Square Kilometre Array (SKA) precursor array that will form an integral part of phase 1 of the SKA. The telescope is located in the central Karoo in South Africa and the site is briefly described. The dish and feed, correlator and overall array design are discussed, as is calibration, imaging and RFI mitigation. MeerKAT as an example of mission driven innovation is considered. Planned MeerKAT science is briefly outlined. The paper concludes with a summary of plans for SKA phases 1 and 2.

articleTitle: A novel lower frequency dual-polarized broadband horn antenna for use as a source in tapered anechoic chambers
abstract: A novel dual-polarized broadband horn antenna working at 75-500 MHz with coaxial input feed section is investigated. Some new structures are introduced to support the huge dimensions and reduce the weight based on the precondition that the effect of these solutions to the low end performance is minimization. And an adjustable shorting plate is inserted on the bottom of the horn antenna to improve the return loss performance. Details of the horn antenna design and experimental results are presented and discussed.

articleTitle: A dualband microstrip antenna for wearable application
abstract: In this paper an h type dualband microstrip antenna fed by a 50 Ω microstrip transmission line is presented for wearable application in the ISM band (2.4-2.5 GHz, 5.725-5.875 GHz). The proposed antenna has two paths for the current, so we can get the dual band performance. As for the wearable application, we use a felt as the substrate to make sure the antenna can bend follow human body. The first band is about 2.4% for the center frequency of 2.45 GHz and the second band extends from 5.735 to 6.015 GHz with a fractional bandwidth of 6.4%. The overall size of the proposed antenna is 70mm*40mm*3mm. Details of the simulated and measured results are presented and discussed.

articleTitle: Modified design of the antipodal Vivaldi antenna
abstract: A modified Vivaldi antenna operating at a frequency range of 0.5 to 3 GHz with lower cut-off frequency and higher low frequency gain than the conventional one is proposed. A current choke structure composed of a set of rectangular gratings that etched on the Vivaldi antenna prototype was introduced in the improved antenna to achieve the purpose of reducing the cut-off frequency and increasing the gain at the low end of operating band. FDTD method was used in the current choke structure optimizing work. Measured results show that compared with a conventional Vivaldi antenna without the current choke structure, the cut off frequency and gain of this novel antenna at low frequency band is 130 MHz lower and about 3.1dB higher, respectively.

articleTitle: A novel application of frequency selective surface in dual-band WLAN antenna
abstract: In this paper, combined elements method is introduced to achieve dual stop-band frequency selective surface (FSS). Later, a dual-band WLAN antenna is designed and the centre frequency is at 2.4GHz and 5.4GHz which accord with the FSS in this paper. We use FSS as dual-band WLAN antenna's reflection plan to improve the performance of antenna. The analysis and results of antenna and FSS are given. The results show that antenna's gain can be improved after the FSS is placed as the reflection plane. This is a new research area which have great prospect in the design of antenna combined with FSS.

articleTitle: A triband short-circuited suspended solar patch antenna
abstract: In this paper, a triband low-profile short-circuited suspended patch antenna combined with a polycrystalline silicon solar cell working as a radiating patch element is proposed for 2.3/2.5/2.8/3.3/3.5 GHz band WiMAX and 2.4 GHz band WLAN networks. The fabricated multifunctional solar antenna offers measured impedance bandwidths of 230, 130 and 280 MHz at the resonance frequencies of 2.4, 2.8 and 3.45 GHz with measured gains of 7.4, 7.8 and 7.6 dBi respectively. The proposed solar antenna generates a measured open circuit voltage of 0.595 V with a short circuit current of 602 mA as a result of the photovoltaic effect, operating with a calculated solar efficiency of 13.22% and providing a DC power output of 0.238 W.

articleTitle: A novel planar UWB antenna with triple band-notched characteristics
abstract: A novel circular-fan-shaped ultra wideband (UWB) printed planar antenna with triple band-notched characteristics is proposed and discussed in detail. The realization of the proposed antenna's triple band-notched characteristics is owed to slots on the ground plane and the radiating patch. By employing a curve-shaped defected ground structure (DGS) on the ground plane, a notched band of 8.0-8.4 GHz is achieved. By embedding a curve-shaped slot and playground-shaped slot on the radiating patch, we get another two notched bands: 3.3-3.6 GHz and 5.1-5.8 GHz. The proposed antenna has been successfully simulated, fabricated, and measured. Moreover, the antenna has a small size, which is benefit for UWB communication system.

articleTitle: Antenna array design in MIMO radar using cyclic difference sets and genetic algorithm
abstract: This paper addresses the issue of how to properly arrange the transmitting and receiving (Tx/Rx) antenna elements of MIMO radar in order to achieve the best spatial resolution. By combining the positive features of cyclic difference sets (CDSs) and genetic algorithm (GA), a hybrid optimization method is proposed for the optimal design of MIMO radar arrays. Numerical results are also presented, showing the variety in array configurations and notable improvement in the spatial resolution.

articleTitle: Application in low-frequency ground-wave propagation of parallel FDTD based on GPU
abstract: The parallel FDTD technique based on the graphics processing unit (GPU) is used to predict the low-frequency (LF) ground-wave propagation over irregular terrains in this paper. First of all, through comparing the prediction results of the smooth earth computed by the serial FDTD algorithm, the technique is verified. Then, with the specific examples, the speedup performance of the parallel algorithm is analyzed. The simulation results show that: the technique can improve the calculation speed greatly for long-distance ground-wave propagation problems. It provides an effective solution for the FDTD application in the wave propagation prediction of large-scale.

articleTitle: Scattering of a high-order Bessel beam by a sphere
abstract: The rigorous theory for the scattering of a high-order Bessel beam (HOBB) by a sphere is presented. The Beam Shape Coefficients (BSCs) for HOBB are calculated using Integral Localized Approximation (ILA), and the scattering coefficients are expanded using Debye series (DSE). The far-field scattered intensities are simulated, and the effect of angle of axicon and the order of HOBB on the scattered intensity is studied.

articleTitle: Progress of UHF/VHF plasma antenna research
abstract: Plasma antenna has characteristics such as low RCS, reconfigurable, etc. But compared with common metal antenna, it has larger size and weight and need extra exciting RF power. In plasma antenna research, the most serious problem is the antenna gain which is difficult to compare with common metal antennas. This article introduces the plasma antenna progress of the Chinese Academy of Science, which has begun this theme since 2004. In our research, we have got good antenna gain and pattern parameters that are very close to metal antennas.

articleTitle: Study on performance of M-ary PPM underwater optical communication systems using vector radiative transfer theory
abstract: The frequency response model for the underwater wireless optical communication channel is obtained using the discrete ordinates method based on vector radiative transfer theory. And the performance of a 1Gb/s communication system with M-ary PPM has been evaluated by applying this frequency response model. The results show that with the increase of transmission distance the bit-error-rate performance degrades, and the field of view (FOV) has a different behaviour in terms of bit-error-rate performance as distance increases. In short distance, with the increase of FOV the bit-error-rate performance degrades, and in long distance, it is opposite. The 4-PPM bit-error-rate performance is almost equal to that of OOK modulation. 8-PPM or 16-PPM can be used to get more improvement in bit-error-rate performance and higher power efficiency.

articleTitle: Efficient ray-tracing model for propagation prediction for microcellular wireless communication systems
abstract: In this paper, we present a novel heuristic quasi 3-D ray-tracing model by taking into account the advantages of both the image theory and shooting-and-bouncing ray tracing methods. This new model is based on preorder-creating a new visibility virtual source tree together with modified polar sweep algorithm. As it is fundamentally a point-to-point ray tracing method and efficient acceleration techniques are introduced, all possible ray paths in the environment microcell can be found and the reduction of the numbers of intersection calculation can also be achieved. Meanwhile, the proposed method can avoid memory leaks and increase the accuracy of the prediction. The prediction results by this new model are compared with published reference, which indicates the improved model bears higher efficiency and precision.

articleTitle: Characteristic of time-varying plasma sheath channel
abstract: It has been mentioned in several literatures that the plasma sheath is time-varying, which could be treated as a time-varying communication channel from the point view of communication and signal characteristic. A mathematical channel model is proposed with a dynamic stratified modelling method, and the channel characteristic features such as coherence bandwidth and coherence time are analysed in this paper. These channel characteristics are important in the selection and design of the communication system including the best transmitted data rate.

articleTitle: Direct solution of electromagnetic scattering using CBFM with ACA algorithm
abstract: The adaptive cross approximation (ACA) algorithm enhanced characteristic basis function method (CBFM) is studied in this article. The ACA algorithm is employed not only to fast calculate off-diagonal submatrices of the reduced matrix, but also to efficiently generate the CBFs and the diagonal submatrices of the reduced matrix, which makes the new method more efficient. Numerical results about the electromagnetic scattering from perfect electric conducting (PEC) targets are given to demonstrate the merits of the new method.

articleTitle: Omnidirectional antenna with dipole array
abstract: An omnidirectional antenna is presented. It is composed of dipole array. This antenna operates at 2.4 GHz for WLAN. As the radiation element, the dipole has a minimized height for reducing the size of antenna. Its size is 27mm high and 75mm length. Four dipoles that encircle a metal cylinder at the radial direction form an omnidirectional element. Along the axial direction there are three omnidirectional elements with the distance of 101mm. The gain of this antenna is 7.1 dBi at 2.4 GHz and the gain variation in azimuth plane less than 0.5dB.

articleTitle: The theoretical and experimental study on backscattering from arable land
abstract: Influence of frequency, incident angle, soil dielectric on backscattering coefficient from cropland is analyzed. By using Small Slope Approximation (SSA) method, we calculate backscattering coefficient with different frequency and polarization, and compare the results with the experimental data. In addition, the Morchin model and Ulaby Model are introduced to examine the numerical results of SSA.

articleTitle: Study of WPT system for charging portable devices on a desk
abstract: Wireless power transfer (WPT) is interesting again because it is an effective technology to realize the ubiquitous society. WPT via magnetic resonant coupling is a new technology which power can be transferred via coupled magnetic resonant in the non-radiative near-field. A simple wireless desktop charging system via coupled magnetic resonant was proposed in this paper. This system contains two same structure minimize antennas which was embedded into the monitor and the portable electronic devices. The transfer efficiency related with different transfer conductions was simulated and analysed. Experimental results show that the power transfer efficiency is more than 70% when the distance between two antennas are 30mm. The receiving antenna can be also used as a communication antenna because the reflection coefficient of antenna is low when antenna resonant at high communication frequency bandwidth of UHF.

articleTitle: The analysis and comparison of the electromagnetic radiation characteristic of the Koch fractal dipole antennas
abstract: The electromagnetic radiation characteristic of the Koch fractal dipole antenna is analyzed, the logical assumption that the current along the Koch fractal dipole antenna obeys sine distribution is demonstrated, and the approximate expression of the magnetic vector potential of the Koch fractal dipole antenna is obtained. Using the magnetic vector potential, the far electromagnetic field is simulated, and the simulated results are compared with those obtained from the traditional symmetrical dipole antenna. For electrically large or electrically equivalent antennas, the results indicate that the electrical length of the Koch fractal dipole antenna has little influence on the radiation patterns. By using of this conclusion, the size of antennas can be reduced, as well as the least gain of antenna is satisfied. Therefore, it will be good for analytical design of multi-band and multi-functional antennas using fractal geometries. Finally, the rationalities of formulas and computations are validated by CST simulation.

articleTitle: Compact dual-band loop-loaded monopole with integrated band-select filter for WLAN application
abstract: A compact loop-loaded dual-band monopole with integrated band-select filter for 2.45/5.2-GHz wireless local area network (WLAN) is presented. The proposed integrated antenna system comprises a loop-loaded dual-band monopole radiator and a microstrip dual-band pseudo-interdigital bandpass filter. Instead of using the traditional 50Ω interfaces, the impedance between the filter and antenna is optimized to improve the performance. The proposed integrated antenna system provides good selectivity and rejection in out of band regions and omnidirectional radiation patterns within the two desired bands. The measured results show good agreement with the simulated ones.

articleTitle: 2D simulation of a SiGe HBT based on energy balance model
abstract: An implementation of the energy balance (EB) model is presented to describe energy transport in heterostructure transistors in this paper. As an application, a 2D simulation of a SiGe heterostructure bipolar transistor (HBT) is carried out. Some typical numerical results are presented, such as the I-V curve, distribution of electron density, current density and electron temperature, etc. Compared with the classical drift diffusion (DD) model, the EB model gives more accurate results at the cost of time and space complexity.

articleTitle: Study on cloud processing with MODIS data and application
abstract: Due to the influence of atmosphere condition, cloud cover is one of the most disturbance factors in remote sensing image. So cloud detection and removal is a very important step for improving the quality of the image before making analysis. In this paper, the multispectral cloud detection algorithm based on spectral character and threshold is used to detect cloud, then in order to make up for the defects of different removing cloud methods, different methods to remove the cloud in images should be used according to different cloud thickness. The improved homomorphic filter algorithm and replacement method are selected to remove cloud in MODIS images. It is found that the effect of removing cloud is very significant. Finally, cloud processing is applied to the inversion of sea-surface temperature (SST).

articleTitle: Use grey system theory to analyze EMI harmonic spectrum
abstract: During equipment level electromagnetic interference (EMI) experiment, there always exist some frequency spectrum that excess the emission limit, among which harmonic spectrum is the major component. This paper puts forward a method to specially analyze the EMI harmonic spectrum, using model of grey system theory to construct grey-period model for the EMI harmonic spectrum, and the model turns out to include the total trend component and the harmonic component. This paper also testifies the method in actual test, the result shows that the model accuracy can reach 97%, and it extracts the harmonic component effectively, so that this method can be used to describe the EMI harmonic spectrum and find the harmonic component to make support for the electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) design.

articleTitle: New design of ultra-wideband bandpass filter using interdigitated coupled lines CRLH-TL structure
abstract: The interest in UWB communication systems using metamaterial concept has been significant increased. In this paper, an ultra wideband bandpass filter based on composite right/left transmission line is presented. The proposed UWB bandpass filter is obtained by cascading the interdigital lines and three units of DGS structure. For the designed BPF, a wide bandwidth is achieved ranging from 3.9 to 10.3GHz. Moreover, the insertion loss is less than 1.5dB and the return loss better than −10dB, confirmed by measurement.

articleTitle: A model for remote sensing sea level with GPS interferometric signals using RHCP antenna
abstract: Determination of tides using reflected signals is an important aspect of GNSS application technique at the present. For the problem of remote sensing the tide heights, a method of retrieving the height of sea surface is proposed from the power of the interference signals obtained by a coastal GPS receiver with singular antenna. An experiment was carried out at the coast of Qingdao. Results of the receiving antenna height over the sea surface from observed interference signals are presented. Compared to tide gauges, the results show its validity of the method based on GPS interference measurements using right-hand circular polarization antenna.

articleTitle: The synthesis of a longitudinal slot array on a rectangular waveguide
abstract: Rectangular waveguide slot array antenna has the advantages of high gain, lowside lobe and small size. These advantages are satisfied with the demand of airborne radar and ship borne radar. In this paper, we discuss the design of longitudinal slots in rectangular waveguide. The method of Taylor synthesize has been used in the process of design. This method doesn't has the limit of slot compare with the method of Chebyshevsynthesize. Through calculation by means of programming, we can get the excitation of every slot. Then we can compute other parameters through the way which Stevenson had put forward. And finally, we can simulate the model created by the parameters calculated till all the indexes meet the requirements of the design.

articleTitle: Maximum capacity antenna design for an indoor MIMO-UWB communication system
abstract: In this paper, the synthesis of scenario-based capacity maximizing/optimal antennas for an indoor MIMO-UWB system is presented. Since the wavelength changes significantly across the whole spectrum, a solution must be found in order to utilize the same optimal antenna configuration for the whole UWB band. A systematic framework is presented here whereby the optimal outcome with orthogonal channels is guaranteed. The synthesis also aids in reducing the number of antenna elements needed contrary to the traditional antenna array used in MIMO systems. The resulting optimal radiation pattern and its capacity analysis are also shown.

articleTitle: Design of a novel monopole antenna with 5.5 GHz band-notch characterization for UWB applications
abstract: In this paper, a new ultra-wideband (UWB) monopole antenna with band-notch characteristic is presented. This antenna is designed to cover the federal communications commission (FCC) bandwidth for UWB applications (3.1-10.6 GHZ) with WLAN frequency band rejection. The band-notch effect is obtained by introducing a U-shaped slot on the radiating part of the antenna.

articleTitle: Plasma sheath phase fluctuation and its effect on GPS navigation
abstract: The plasma sheath can potentially degrade electromagnetic systems through signal attenuation as well as increased amplitude and phase fluctuation. Utilizing electron density and collision frequency provided by NASA, transmission coefficient is calculated by the scattering matrix method and phase fluctuation is obtained. By means of Electromagnetic propagation theory and GPS software receiver, the effects of phase fluctuation by plasma sheath on GPS signal and its positioning are analyzed. Results show that the maximal percentage of variation larger than 5m is up to 14%.

articleTitle: Non-invasive breast cancer thermotherapy studies using conformal microstrip antennas
abstract: In this paper, a circular and a toroidal conformal microstrip antenna are proposed for a simplified non-invasive microwave breast cancer therapy and the Specific Absorption Rate (SAR) in the breast and heart model is analyzed based on the simulated results by HFSS using Finite Element Method (FEM). Different schemes of antenna ground plane are considered in the simulation to find the best focusing effects in the tumor region. By comparing the simulation results, the conclusion can be drawn that the focusing effect in tumor region is enhanced when the size of antenna ground decreases. Moreover, the toroidal antenna with inner radius of 15mm has a better focusing effect when antenna shape changes from circular to toroidal. In the meantime, the SAR value in heart region is much smaller than that in breast region, i.e. heart is in good condition.

articleTitle: Study on the optics of the 5 meter Dome A Terahertz Explorer (DATE5) for Antarctica
abstract: The 5 m Dome A Terahertz Explorer (DATE5) is a proposed terahertz telescope to be deployed in Dome A, Antarctica, to exploit one of the best observing conditions at terahertz bands on the earth. This paper presents a study on the optics of the proposed DATE5 antenna. Two configurations, namely the Cassegrain and the Coudé configurations, are proposed and their respective optical performances, such as field of view, beam and aperture efficiency, and chopping performance, are simulated and compared. Some engineering considerations, such as system reliability and environmental adaptability are also discussed.

articleTitle: Modelling on the signal BER of communication system for high-speed railway
abstract: During the process of high-speed railway running, the modulated signals of different frequencies show much more multi-path fading degree because of the Doppler shift. The bit error rate (BER) characteristics of signal are different from that at low-speed. The BER has a significant impact on the reliability of wireless mobile communication system. A wireless channel model is formulated include large scale effects and fading caused by randomness and multipath encountered under high speed railway environment, and used for the estimation to the BER of two advanced modulation system, GSM-R and TETRA, for high-speed railway systems. The effects of the different railway speed and different signal frequency to the wireless radio BER are analysed based on the simulated results.

articleTitle: Millimetre-wave all symmetric edge-coupled bandpass filter
abstract: The design of an all symmetric edge-coupled bandpass filter (BPF) at Ka band is presented. Effects of manufacturing tolerances on the design of the edge-coupled bandpass filter are investigated. Consequently, a procedure is devised for a first pass design of such filters. The open-end effect in the half-wavelength resonator section is compensated with the round-ended corners rather than decrementing the lengths in a conventional way. The widths of all the half-wavelength resonators are set equal to avoid discontinuities in the interior of the filter. The fabrication tolerances are compensated in the design prior to manufacturing. The filter is realized on a ceramic filled soft substrate with dielectric constant of 6.2. An in-house customized through-reflect-line (TRL) calibration kit is produced to obtain the de-embedded measured results at the device plane. The measured results are in good agreement with the simulated results. The insertion loss is 3 dB, passband variation is less than 1 dB and the filter exhibits 3dB bandwidth of 3.8 GHz.

articleTitle: A novel reconfigurable notch-band UWB antenna
abstract: In this paper, we present a novel ultra-wideband (UWB) antenna with the reconfigurable notch band. The proposed antenna consists of an elliptical-shaped patch, a 50-Ohm CPW feed line, and a tapered ground plane. To obtain reconfigurable notch band, the ring-shaped slot structure with several switches is added into the patch. Effect of several antenna design parameters on the input and radiation performance is discussed in detail. As an example, the two-notch-band UWB antenna (3.3GHz~3.6GHz, 5.15GHz~5.825GHz) is fabricated and measured by using zero-Ohm resistor.

articleTitle: A calculation model and characteristics analysis of radio wave propagation in rectangular shed tunnel
abstract: Shed tunnel belongs to a kind of heterogeneous tunnel of open cut tunnel, which has been widely used in the railway as well as highway construction. Geometrical optics method is adopted in this paper to study and present a simulation of radio waves propagation in rectangular shed tunnels. By comparing the received power under different polarization modes, frequencies and permittivities, we get some relevant conclusions that the near-field region signal in shed tunnel fade soon, and the vertical polarization radio wave propagate in the shed tunnel is greatly influenced by environment.

articleTitle: A novel method to eliminate ionospheric phase contamination in OTHR systems
abstract: In over-the-horizon radar (OTHR), radar signals are subjected to ionosphere perturbation as they propagate through the ionosphere, and the weak echo signal from the low-speed target is almost masked by the spreading of Bragg peak. In order to acquire the spread sea clutter accurately, sliding window band-pass filters is proposed to extract the first order clutter (calibration signal), which can realize adaptive selection of the filter bandwidth. At the same time, a novel algorithm named Covariance Matrix Solving method (CMS) is presented to correct ionospheric phase contamination. Theoretical analysis and real data processing indicate that CMS method has a good performance and can obtain a better correction effect than Phase Gradient Autofocus (PGA) method.

articleTitle: Dual-wideband, dual-polarized shared aperture antenna with high isolation and low cross-polarization
abstract: This paper describes the design of a dual-wideband dual linear polarization shared aperture patch antenna. The antenna consists of one antenna element for L-band and an 8×8 planar array for X-band, sharing the same radiation aperture. The array, together with the feeding network is analyzed with HFSS software. The Return Loss, Isolation, and Radiation Patterns of the array are presented. The impedance bandwidth of this antenna array, corresponding to 10dB Return Loss is 13.0% and 14.7% in L- and X-band respectively. The isolation between the orthogonal polarization ports is better than 25 dB and 35 dB in L- and X-band respectively. The cross-polarization is below -22 dB and -25 dB in L- and X-band respectively.

articleTitle: Research of communication equipments mutual interference in complicated electromagnetic environment
abstract: The mutual interference of different frequency devices is one of key problems to the effectiveness evaluation of electronic information equipment test in complicated electromagnetic environment. The mechanism is analysed and extensive tests are carried on. The test results show that the stray signal, harmonic and intermodualtion interference have more effect on normal communication.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic pulse protection requirments and test methods for systems
abstract: Electromagnetic pulse (EMP) radiation may seriously threaten the electronic equipments and systems. The EMP energy could be coupled into inside of systems from antennas, cables and apertures, and this would result in the system disturbed even destroyed. The EMP coupling characteristics of different channels are analyzed in this paper, and the general protection requirements for different types of coupling path are investigated. Based on the electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) requirements and test methods for systems and subsystems, the EMP protection test methods combined with radiation and injection for systems are proposed in this paper.

articleTitle: A novel monopole antenna for digital television receiving application
abstract: A wideband operating antenna for digital television (DTV) in the 530–880 MHz band is presented. The proposed antenna has a planar rectangular radiating patch, in which a bended slit is inserted. The bended slit separates the rectangular patch into three subpatches. The defect ground structure is used for size reduction and impedance matching. The simulation results indicate that the proposed antenna is applicable to mobile and digital television (DTV) broadcast signal reception.

articleTitle: A novel low-profile high-gain antenna based on artificial magnetic conductor for LTE applications
abstract: This paper presents a novel low-profile and high-gain antenna which adopts an artificial magnetic conductor (AMC) ground plane as its reflecting surface. Here, the traditional printed dipole antenna is oriented horizontally over the AMC surface which is consisted of 5*7 square plum-shaped patches unit without vertical via to the ground. The optimized antenna has a height about 9.5mm and its peak gain is closed to 9.7dB at 2.58GHz. Moreover, the operating frequency range is from 2.47GHz to 2.77GHz, its relative bandwidth achieves about 11.63%.

articleTitle: A compact UWB BPF design using silicon-based IPD technology
abstract: Band pass filter (BPF) is widely used in the front end of ultra wide band (UWB) system. The miniaturization for the BPF is needed greatly in order to reduce the size and the cost. In this paper we present a compact BPF which is made by using integrated passive device (IPD) technology in high resistance silicon substrate. The filter can achieve the similar performance with smaller size comparing to traditional technologies such as PCB or LTCC. The size of the filter is only 1.53mm×1.09mm. The in-band insertion loss is less than 0.3dB at 7.656GHz with 528MHz bandwidth. Out-band attenuations are more than 20dB in both 6.956GHz and 8.356GHz. Out-band attenuations are more than 20dB in both 6.956GHz and 8.356GHz.

articleTitle: A new method for ionospheric short-term forecast using similar-day modeling
abstract: The conception of similar-day and its modelling of ionospheric short-term forecast are presented. The similar-day method not only has the merits of simpleness and facility, but also improves the forecast accuracy. A test of the method for 1h∼24h f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>F<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> forecast of Manzhouli, Beijing, Urumchi and Haikou during the periods of the high level solar activities (in 1980) and a comparison with the autocorrelation method developed by LIU R show that the method is realistic and reliable. The similar-day method betters the forecast result obviously for more than N h ahead (N=1 for winter and equinoxes, N=3 for summer), and especially in winter, the relative error can be usually reduced by 2 percent or so. Finally, a new method for ionospheric short-term forecast is formed by combining the similar-day method and the autocorrelation method.

articleTitle: A magnetically resonant coupling system for wireless power transmission
abstract: Magnetically resonant coupling is a steady and feasible approach for wireless power transmission (WPT), also called contactless power transfer. This paper presents a process to design a complete WPT system which can be connected to daily alternating current (AC) power source directly. Subsequently, by comparative simulation and experimental analysis between circular coil pair and octagonal coil pair on the printed circuit board (PCB) reaches the conclusion that the former has better performance in the WPT unit system. Each pair is measured by the vector network analyser (VNA) to acquire the values of serial resistance, mutual inductance and self inductance. These parameters can be set into Advanced Design System (ADS) to find the operating characteristics of the resonance circuit and the power efficiency of the coil pair system. With this simulation and experiment in PCB coil pairs, the complete WPT system including AC-direct current (DC) converter, primary driven circuit, PCB circular coil pair spaced 15 mm apart and secondary rectifier circuit is designed and tested. The whole system achieves a power transmission efficiency of approximate 50% at the frequency of 500 KHz.

articleTitle: GPS-based ionospheric tomography with constrained IRI as a regularization
abstract: Recent developments in ionosphere remote sensing, in particular techniques using the global positioning system (GPS) provide an unprecedented capability for monitoring the state of the ionosphere, its reaction to solar-terrestrial events as well as ionospheric wave phenomena. There have been many methods that were suggested to study the feasibility of using the International Reference Ionosphere (IRI) model as a regularization profile for ionospheric tomography experiments. Due to the limited-angle geometry, the vertical precision of ground-based GPS ionospheric tomography still needs to be improved to meet the requirements of some applications, such as monitoring the ionospheric distributions during the ionospheric storm periods. HmF2 (peak height of F2 layer of ionosphere) obtained by vertical soundings as a constrained parameter to IRI will improve the vertical resolution of the ground-base GPS ionospheric tomography. Vertical and oblique sounding data obtained from CRIRP while TEC data obtained from a meridional chain of 6 GPS satellite receivers located in China are used for reconstruction of the mid and low latitude ionosphere, maximum entropy regularization method was used to solve the discrete ill-posed problems, numerical simulations show that the constrained IRI has the potential of becoming a effective regularization profile for ground-based GPS ionospheric tomographic reconstruction of the ionosphere. It has also been observed that the foF2 values obtained from reconstructed images that use constrained IRI as a regularization profile are closer to measured values than those obtained from the images reconstructed with the original IRI regularization profile.

articleTitle: Analysis and improvement of the frequency sweeping method for resonance characteristic measurement
abstract: Two improved methods of accurate measurement of resonant devices' resonance characteristic are presented. One method is based on variable sampling rate and point number, the other is the system function of the resonance. Compared these two methods, the system function of the resonance completely eliminates the frequency spectrum leakage, and then proves the correctness of this method by theory and experiment. The results show that the method of the system function of the resonance greatly improves the measuring accuracy as the same as the good real-time and realizability.

articleTitle: Synthesis of a plane-wave via linear array with unequal interval
abstract: The quality of the quasi-plane wave synthesized in the body under test zone is important in accurate near-field antenna measurements or near-field scattering measurements. In this paper, a linear array made up of infinitely long current filaments is utilized as the theoretical model of plane wave synthesis. Genetic Algorithm(GA) is used to optimize the amplitude and phase distribution of the linear array, and the locations of the elements are considered in the global optimizations. The results of computer simulation show that the uniform degree of the amplitude and phase of the quasi-plane wave synthesized in the near zone of the linear array can be effectively improved by the optimization of the positions of linear array elements by means of GA.

articleTitle: Gain enhancement of axial-mode helical antenna with a cylindrical ring
abstract: This paper proposed a helical antenna with a cylindrical ring above the antenna along the axial direction. Compared with the traditional helical antenna gain boosting techniques, without adding coil number, the gain of the proposed antenna is enhanced by a maximum of 3.8dB in the working bandwidth by adding a cylindrical ring, while the impedance matching bandwidth and other antenna characteristics remain.

articleTitle: The simulation of microstrip Band Pass Filters based on ADS
abstract: Microwave filters are the indispensable part of modern wireless communications, microwave satellite communications and electronic against systems. The advantages of microstrip Band Pass Filter (BPF) are that it is easy in integrating with other RF circuits, that convenient in designing, that small in size and that low in insertion loss. So, it is widely used in RF circuits. This paper will design two types of microstrip BPF, one is the narrow-band BPF use parallel coupled microstrip with one fourth of a wavelength, and the other one is the board-band BPF use stub lines and connecting lines both with a quarter of a wavelength. The paper also simulates and optimizes the filters with ADS (Advanced Design System). The simulation result can satisfy the demand of design.

articleTitle: Comparison of evaporation duct models with meteorology grads tower measurements
abstract: The performance and reliability of microwave radar and communication systems are affected by the so-called evaporation ducts over the sea surface. Usually, the evaporation duct height can be determined using evaporation duct model from measured atmospheric pressure, air temperatures, air humidity and wind speed at a single height within the atmospheric surface layer, and sea surface temperature. Evaporation duct heights which are determined from five evaporation duct models using bulk measurements are compared with data from meteorology grads tower which was founded in Bohai Sea. It is shown that, in the same case of atmospheric stratification, the heights of ducts computed by different models are difference. Recommendations for selection of optimal models are given.

articleTitle: Anti-jamming performance simulation of tactical data link communication system
abstract: The impact of interference on tactical data link communication system (TDLCS) can be quantitatively described through anti-jamming performance simulation. Therefore, anti-jamming performance simulation of TDLCS is of special interest. The developing status of TDLCS and its simulation technique were introduced. Furthermore, the key anti-jamming techniques of Joint Tactical Information Distribution System (JTIDS) for Link 16 were stressed, including channel coding technique, spread spectrum technique and modulation technique. Then link-level simulation model of JTIDS based on the Simulink platform was established. With this model its anti-jamming performance was analyzed. The research results could be applied in the quantitative evaluation of performance effect for TDLCS suffering from radio-frequency interference (RFI) and optimization design of anti-jamming or jamming strategy for TDLCS.

articleTitle: A preliminary study of the NeQuick model over China using GPS TEC and ionosonde data
abstract: This paper presents a preliminary study of the NeQuick model over 3 stations in China, Changchun, Beijing and Chongqing for geomagnetic quiet days. In order to understand its weaknesses and validate its results, we chose to uncouple NeQuick formulation from its underlying data. It is found that NeQuick represents NmF2 and VTEC quite well on monthly average, except for some underestimate. After replacing the CCIR maps of NmF2 and M(3000)F2 by its DGS measurements, the model behaves even better. Based on these results, we conclude that: (1) NeQuick represents ionosphere quite well over China on monthly average. (2) NeQuick has the ability to accommodate other sources of data for its crucial parameters, such as DGS measurement. (3) NeQuick has the potential to represent ionosphere on daily or sub-daily average.

articleTitle: Research on grating lobe suppression based on the virtual array transformation algorithm
abstract: In beamforming, the grating lobe is produced when the element spacing is increased to more than 1/2 wavelength. This paper outlines the mechanism of producing grating lobe and summarizes the used technologies of grating lobe suppression. Considering the issue of grating lobe suppression, this paper analyses the feasibility of ambiguity solving with virtual elements using the virtual array transformation algorithm and the virtual array algorithm based on least squares estimator. We use the least squares algorithm to estimate the received data of virtual elements between the adjacent elements based on the known received data of actual elements, and to reduce the spacing which can be set as 1/2 wavelength without change the actual aperture of antenna array, thus the grating lobes is suppressed. Simulation results verify the feasibility of the algorithm.

articleTitle: Design of a new type of the damped filter for system stability of DC-DC converter
abstract: Based on a series R-C damping circuit used to stabilize the whole system, a new type of damped filter is proposed, and the expressions of the optimal damping design are deduced. Moreover, the blocking capacitance is much smaller than the parallel R-C damping circuit proposed in previous literature. The new type of filter used for the input and output filter of the buck converter is benefit to maintain the stability of the system and a smooth output waveform. The advantages of the new type of filter are illustrated and verified by MATLAB/Simulink.

articleTitle: Shielding effectiveness calculation of metallic enclosure with aperture array
abstract: As an equipment protecting and isolating electromagnetic interference, the shielding enclosure always needs aperture on the wall which destroys the completeness of the enclosure. In this article, the transmission line method (TL method) is applied in the electromagnetic shielding effectiveness (SE) of a metallic enclosure with aperture array. We analysed the situation of incident arbitrary polarized electromagnetic wave, the number and arrangement of aperture array, and give the equivalent calculation expression when the number of side holes, length of aperture arrays ranging. At last, we give the recommendations of the relationship between the hole size and the distance between apertures by simulation. Good agreement are obtained between simulated results and calculated results.

articleTitle: A novel miniaturized Frequency Selective Surface
abstract: Frequency Selection Surface are employed in a variety of electromagnetic application, such as radomes (terrestrial and airborne), electromagnetic shielding absorbers and antennas. etc, this article discuss a new method of miniaturized FSS, unlike the others, cells of this new FSS is composing two layer of metallic patch with a thin medium between. The distributed capacitance of the periodic cell is formed by the coupling of the two metallic patches in different layers. Simulations of the important design variables are presented and a unit cell size of λ/16 is proposed.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic situation representation based on parallel coordinates and radial coordinates
abstract: The representation of electromagnetic situation (EMS) is a key step in spectrum management and decision support in battlefield. In the past, 2-D and 3-D visualization methods were the only options for electromagnetic environment representation, but the complexity of electromagnetic environment of modern battlefield demands for a higher level of visualization of massinformation. Thus, we propose a new method to visualize EMS based on multi-dimension information visualization technology. To achieve this, we represent several key factors of electromagnetic field in a multi-dimensional coordinate system, and the corresponding domains are visually presented by the introduced parallel coordinates and radial coordinates. Simulation results show that this method can illustrate the EMS in a single coordinate effectively, which could provide excellent decision supporting and plan-aiding for users.

articleTitle: Effect study of spectrum analyzer noise floor on antenna noise temperature measurement
abstract: In this paper, Y-factor method of measuring antenna noise temperature is described simply using spectrum analyzer. Effect of spectrum analyzer noise floor on noise power measurement is analyzed. Calculation formula and numerical value curve of correction factor are given. Calculation of correction Y-factor is described. At fast, measuring results of C-band 13-metre vehicle antenna noise temperature are given. Test result show that effect of spectrum analyzer noise floor on antenna noise measurement is not neglected when ratio of spectrum analyzer measuring noise power to noise floor power is less than 20dB.

articleTitle: Two kinds of dual-band power amplifier matching networks using three-section microstrip line
abstract: This paper presents two kinds of dual-band power amplifier matching networks, which using three-section microstrip line. Based on the analysis of transmission line theory, two matching networks used in dual-band amplifier are introduced: Multi-section Transmission Line (MSTL) and Open Stub Transmission Line (OSTL). After a series of calculations and simulation, those two structures have been successfully designed. In order to prove that the structures are applicable to the dual-band power amplifier, a dual-band power amplifier using those structures is proposed. Based on experimental results, the amplifier, which works at 915MHz and 2140MHz, achieves efficiency of more than 60%. When input power is 30dBm, with output of 46dBm, the gain compressed is 1.8dB at 2140HMz and 2.2dB at 915HMz.

articleTitle: A broadband bow-tie antenna used in UHF with metal reflection plane
abstract: There are many kinds of antennas used in UWB system. Double-side printed bow-tie antenna is one of them which has the advantages of light weight, planar structure, low cost and broad bandwidth. In this paper, a double-side printed bow-tie antenna used in UHF band is proposed first. Then a metal reflection plane is added on the back of this antenna to increase its gain and inhibit backward radiation. Return loss of -10dB or better is located in the band of 0.95-2.7 GHz and the relative bandwidth is 95.9%. They have the similar VSWR quality. Besides, the reflection plane has a strong influence on radiation pattern and antenna gain. Gain in dB of former antenna has been raised from around 2.5dB to 7.5dB due to the metal reflection plane. Hence, it has a great prospect in the application of double-side printed bow-tie antenna with metal reflection plane.

articleTitle: A compact triple-band printed monopole antenna for WLAN/WiMAX applications
abstract: A simple printed triple-band monopole antenna for applications in WLAN and WiMAX band is proposed. The antenna is very compact with a size of 26 × 20 × 1mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> and fed by a 50 Ω microstrip line with a modified ground plane. An experimental prototype has been fabricated and tested. The measured results show good triple-band operation with -10dB impedance bandwidths of the proposed antenna cover 2.38-2.53GHz, 3.37-4.04GHz, and 4.51-6.04GHz, respectively, which meet the required bandwidths specification of 2.4/5GHz WLAN and 3.5/5.5GHz WiMAX standard. In addition, good antenna performances such as radiation patterns and antenna gain over the operating bands have been obtained.

articleTitle: A new compact MIMO antenna design with high isolation for 1710∼2700MHz
abstract: A new compact MIMO antenna layout with high isolation and low cross correlation is proposed. The MIMO antenna comprises two identical antenna elements with couple-fed and inductive shorting strip covering 1710~2700MHz with VSWR 3:1. It achieves the generation of λ/8 resonant mode at about 1.75GHz. Each antenna is placed oppositely at the edge of the system circuit board of the mobile handset with 100*50*1mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>, and occupies a very little volume with 10*20mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> respectively. The measured isolation is better than -20dB and the maximum envelope of the cross correlation is 0.17 over the desired frequency operation, which are very attractive for the present wireless communication commands. Results of simulated and tested are presented and some key parameters are also discussed in this study.

articleTitle: A developed phase differences interpolation algorithm in the correlative interferometer
abstract: A developed phase differences interpolation algorithm in the correlative interferometer is proposed in this paper. Using the phase differences interpolation operation in the follow-up data processing, the improved method could reach a high precision while the process-time is acceptable. Simulation results show that this optimization method works well and has a much higher accuracy than traditional methods.

articleTitle: Simulation analysis of crosstalk and radiation effects of cables inside aerocraft
abstract: There are a lot of electronic equipment on aerocraft, which results that different kinds of cables connect complexly. These have increased the difficulty of the analysis of electromagnetic interference in an aerocraft. The purpose of this paper is on modeling a simple cable harness inside aerocraft and simulating the crosstalk and radiation characteristics with the software CST. It can provide a reference to predict electromagnetic compatibility problems in aerocraft, for the field test is not convenient.

articleTitle: Mutual coupling analysis of Adcock Watson Watt direction finding system based on the receiving mutual impedance
abstract: A new mutual coupling analysis of Adcock antennas in both original and improved Watson Watt direction finding system based on receiving coupling impedance concept is provided. The close electrical spacing of the Adcock antenna elements will introduces some undesirable mutual coupling affects on receiving terminal voltages at the antenna elements. But, by using the symmetry consideration, it is proved that there will be no impact on Direction-Of-Arrival (DOA) estimation accuracy in both original and improved Watson Watt direction finding system. Our simulation results and DOA examples study demonstrate the validity of analysis.

articleTitle: The calculation of infrared radiance of rough sea surface
abstract: Based on the Cox-Munk sea model, we calculate the emissivity of rough sea surface without interaction between the wave facets, and the emissivity of rough sea surface considering about interaction between the wave facets. According to the emissivity of rough sea surface, we compute the radiance diances of rough sea surface based on the two emissivity models at different view angles in the 3-5 micron band and 8-12 micron band respectively. Finally, we obtain that the difference of the radiances is found to be small for small to moderate view angles. For large view angles, the discrepancy of the radiances is large. In the 3-5 micron band, the difference increases with the growth of wavelength, when the wavelength is 5 micron, the difference is 0.0002 w/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.μm.sr, reaching the maximum, In the 8-12 micron band, the maximal discrepancy of the radiances is 0.00091 w/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.μm.sr.

articleTitle: Human-body shadowing modeling for indoor quasi-static MIMO channels
abstract: In recent years, MIMO communication systems such as IMT-Advanced and LTE have been put into practical use. Since MIMO transmission has an advantage in use in the indoor multipath-rich environment, the accurate indoor MIMO channel model is necessary for evaluating the systems. In indoor Quasi-static environment, it is known that the channel state changes dynamically due to the human-body shadowing effect even if the receiver and the transmitter are fixed. We have proposed the estimation method of human-body shadowing of each cluster for MIMO channel modeling. In our proposal, firstly the propagation parameter distributions of clusters are estimated from the data measured in static condition using SAGE and K-Power-Means algorithm. Next, the human-body shadowing of each cluster is estimated from the Beamformer resultant power variations of cluster that are calculated from the data measured in quasi-static condition. We carried out the 3.35GHz measurements in the cafeteria during lunch time. As a result, we showed that shadowing level was from 5dB to 15dB at busy time of cafeteria. In addition, we also showed that the mean decrease and variance of resultant power is almost in the proportional relation.

articleTitle: Array characteristic of the strong-coupling based on even-odd mode technology
abstract: The paper presents the even-odd mode (EOM) analysis technique for array electrical characteristics of strong-coupling in the fired state, and decompose the array port S-parameter within the emission-coupling antenna framework, resulting in odd-mode radiation power and odd-mode impedance. Its significance lies in two kinds of active impedance separation in the strong-coupling array port, and provides a theoretical support for the unit-port matches. Finally, the 180-degree hybrid balun is presents for the realization of the two modes of decomposition, and gives 2×2 array of the experimental and calculated results from the project implementation and application views.

articleTitle: Influence of multiple scattering on rain attenuation
abstract: The effects of varying parameters a<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</inf> and b<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</inf> of different results on rain attenuation are discussed in this paper. With Monte Carlo method, the attenuation of rain medium is simulated and the numerical results considering multiple scattering of rain are compared with that calculated by using IUT-R model. The direction of research on the rain attenuation is indicated.

articleTitle: Generation of local phase model of DOR tones for tracking deep space probes
abstract: In order to track deep space probes with very high accuracy, a type of VLBI technique called Δ DOR (Delta Differential One-way Ranging) has been investigated. The DOR signals emitted by deep space probes usually consist of several tones in a spanned bandwidth that can be extracted by correlation with a locally generated phase model. In this paper the method to generate a nonlinear phase model used for the local correlation of DOR tones is investigated and applied to the processing of a set of DOR data acquired from the ChangE-2 lunar satellite. The observations were conducted by the Chinese VLBI Network in a tracking pass in October 2010. The results indicate that the phase precisions of DOR tones could achieve at about 1 degree with 5s integration time, while the frequency precisions are about 1 mHz.

articleTitle: Planar scissors monopole antenna for UWB communication
abstract: A novel planar scissors monopole antenna for ultrawideband (UWB) communication is presented in this paper. Printed on a dielectric substrate and fed by a 50 microstrip line, a planar scissors monopole has been demonstrated to provide an ultra-wide bandwidth with voltage standing wave ratio (VSWR) less than 2 with satisfactory radiation properties. Details of the antenna design and measured results are presented and discussed. Good agreement is achieved between the simulation and the experiment.

articleTitle: A novel fast measurement method and diagnostic of phased array antennas
abstract: A novel approach composed of the phase-shift measurement method and the encoding matrix is introduced to solve the problem of the fast measurement and the calibration of phased array antennas. Both phased array antennas and probe are fixed in the whole measurement process. The encoding coefficient matrix is used to control the phase-shift of each phase shifter in phased array antennas. The signal of each phase shifter and the excitation of each channel can be recovered after decoding. In the mean time, the fault of each element can be diagnosed. The simulation of the measurement process of the phased array antenna model shows the correctness and effectiveness of the approach.

articleTitle: The synthesis and optimizationof a diplexer for the multi-purpose, multi-frequency shuttlecock antenna
abstract: This paper describes the synthesis procedure and optimization algorithm developed to design a diplexer for the multi-purpose, multi-frequency Shuttlecock antenna. Starting from a low order circuit topology the synthesizer increases the order until the set of specifications are adhered to. The circuit element values are determined by a hybrid optimization algorithm that combines a global search algorithm and a downhill simplex method.

articleTitle: Theory and experiment validation of radio wave propagation in the forest and its application for extended frequency
abstract: A theoretical model for vertical polarized radio wave propagation in the forest is given in this paper. The propagation modes consist of directive wave and reflect wave in the air-forest interface and reflect wave in the forest-ground interface and lateral wave propagating along the upper interface in the air. The expressions of them are given here and the propagation loss can be derived easily from them. And we validate them in the VHF and UHF band using the experiment data measured in typical forest of Central China. Also we extend the formula to the higher frequency such as 1800MHz and 3500MHz. The initial distance where the lateral wave begins to be the predominant propagation mechanism in higher frequency is different from VHF and UHF frequency. It is 600m in 1800MHz and 3500MHz while it is 350m in VHF and UHF band.

articleTitle: Evaluation method of absorber reflectivity using antenna with high reflection coefficient
abstract: In this paper, the evaluation method of absorber reflectivity using the antenna with the high reflection coefficient has been proposed. Since the previously-used equation for calculating the reflectivity of the absorber shows the error when the poorly-mismatched antenna is utilized, the new equation is derived base on the multiple reflection analysis and three simultaneous equations. The derived equation includes the reflection coefficient of the antenna. The proposed method was verified through the simulated results. The method can be easily applied to the product examination by the absorber manufactureras well as the customer because of its simplicity and cost-effectiveness.

articleTitle: A miniature GPS microstrip antenna
abstract: This paper presents a novel structure of the GPS microstrip antenna, the working frequency of the antenna is GPS L1 band (at 1.575 GHz). The top-level patch of the antenna is an irregular shape, this shape is a centre of symmetry, and the purpose of such a design is in order to reduce the size of the antenna under the premise does not affect the antenna performance. Use ANSOFT HFSS simulation software to perform the simulation, the results show that the antenna was able to meet the requirements of the navigation satellite signals.

articleTitle: Research on the DBF method of virtual element interpolation based on end-fire antenna array
abstract: This paper focus on the problem of high side lobes, which will appear near the site of grating lobes in the array factor when enlarging the interval between elements to solve the effect of mutual coupling. It is difficult to meet the requirement of making up antenna array and scanning. In this paper, taking plate end-fire antenna as the array elements arranged along the lateral, axial and two-dimensional directions, CST simulation results and DBF method of virtual element interpolation calculation results of the far field pattern were compared and analyzed. Then, the effectiveness of the DBF method of virtual element interpolation in suppressing the side lobe level was proved. Finally, based on the same computational complexity, non-uniform interpolation was proposed to obtain better far field pattern.

articleTitle: A thinning method of conformal non-concentric circular array using genetic algorithm
abstract: With the development of science and technology, the use of conformal antennas for vehicle applications has been increasing rapidly. And the circular array is widely populated for its all-azimuth scan capability. However, when the landform is restricted, the traditional circular antenna array might not be placed normally. Thus, a special conformal non-concentric circular array which is to put a small circular array into a big circular array is proposed in this paper. The difference of the peak sidelobe level (PSLL) and the main lobe width are considered in order to derive the optimal element number. And a thinning and optimizing approach based on the genetic algorithm for the special antenna is proposed. The simulation results show that the number of antenna array elements can be brought down with simultaneous reduction in the peak sidelobe level with respect to the full array. It will not only increase the efficiency of space utilization, but also improve the system performance.

articleTitle: Characteristics analysis of High-order FDTD method
abstract: A High-order FDTD method has been presented in this paper. The numerical characteristics of the scheme including stability, dispersion and convergence have been investigated. It is observed that the higher order scheme has, the lower numerical dispersion error has, namely, the larger spatial stencil size decrease the numerical dispersion error. Several different cases researches and comparison with the conventional FDTD and the multiresolution time domain (MRTD) methods demonstrate that the High-order FDTD method as a time domain high order method is useful and valuable to study.

articleTitle: A novel 3D ray-tracing model for propagation prediction in indoor environments
abstract: A novel three-dimensional (3D) ray-tracing model for the use of the uniform theory of diffraction and geometrical optics in radio channel characterizations of indoor environments is presented in this paper. The model is based on a technique which multiple reflections, transmissions and diffractions are considered via the ray-path classification into four different categories. And each ray category is determined by using different methods. At last, our theoretical results of the received power are compared with measurements which have been reported. The good agreement with these measurements indicates that our prediction model works well for such indoor communication applications.

articleTitle: Terahertz chiral metamaterial based on complementary U-shaped structure assembly
abstract: In this paper, a terahertz chiral metamaterial (CMM) with complementary U-shaped structure assembly is proposed. The results exhibit that the strong circular dichroism, giant optical activity, and negative refraction could be obtained by numerical simulation and effective EM scattering parameters retrieval method.

articleTitle: Design of circularly polarization H-shaped apertures-coupled microstrip patch antenna array
abstract: A kind of circularly polarized microstrip antenna is designed in S band. The Wilkinson power divider integrated with the microstrip 90 deg phase shifter is used each unit and the patch is coupled by two orthogonal H-shaped, which can enhance the isolation of the two ports and improve the circularly polarized performance. The antenna array gain is about 14 dB. The axial-ratio value within 3dB from −20 deg to 20 deg. The cross-polarization levels in zenith direction are better than −23 dB. This results indicate that the proposed antenna realizes a good circularly polarization performance.

articleTitle: A frequency reconfigurable microwave reaction cavity based on a quarter-wave coaxial cavity resonator
abstract: To investigate the best frequency for a microwave reaction application, a frequency reconfigurable microwave reaction cavity based on the concept of quarter-wave coaxial cavity resonator is proposed and designed. It is able to resonate at different frequency within the bandwidth of 500~1000 MHz by only adjusting the length of the inner conductor and the depth of the feeding structure. This implies a 67% tuneable bandwidth. Within the spherical region with a radius of 50 mm surrounding the inner conductor, the effective value of electric field is greater than 2.6×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sup> V/m for an input excitation of 500 W. As such, a frequency reconfigurable microwave reaction system can be constructed to implement a small scale experiment.

articleTitle: Improvement of 2-D DOA estimation based on L-shaped array
abstract: This paper presents a novel algorithm for two-dimensional (2-D) direction finding based on L-shaped arrays. Firstly, by using the array geometries, four covariance matrices are obtained. Secondly, a particular big matrix constructed by the four covariance matrices is used to estimate the signal subspace. Finally, the direction of arriving angles can be achieved by 2-D ESPRIT algorithm. Simulation results confirm that the proposed method, compared with the conventional methods, has higher estimation accuracy, low computation cost.

articleTitle: Multi-arm spiral metamaterial with electric and magnetic responses
abstract: The design, fabrication and measurement of multi-arm spiral metamaterial are introduced in this paper. The parameter retrieval results and transmission measurement both validate that the multi-arm spiral resonator (SR) have a magnetic and an electric response in the lower and higher frequency regions, which provide us a more convenient way to construct the dual-band left-handed metamaterial (LHM) for more applications in future.

articleTitle: Study of system-level electromagnetic compatibility indicator process based on QFD
abstract: A method of system-electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) indicator process based on quality function deployment (QFD) was built to satisfy the translation from mission to different level of EMC indicator. The input of the QFD - mission importance order was derived via Group analytical hierarchy process (AHP), then with the help of house of quality (HOQ) in the QFD model, indicator importance order can be calculated. After the calculation, fuzzy function was introduced to search the best indicator solution. The whole process of QFD turned the qualitative analyse into quantitative analyse and provide foundation to systemic EMC indicator.

articleTitle: GIM-ingested NeQuick model applied for GPS single frequency ionospheric correction in China
abstract: NeQuick is a semi-empirical model that describes spatial and temporal variations of the ionospheric electron density. This model will be used by the GALILEO single frequency user to compute ionospheric corrections. As a quick-run empirical model, NeQuick can only give the monthly mean variation of the ionosphere that will limit its application for real time single frequency ionospheric correction. However, NeQuick model provides flexible solutions for ingest ionospheric information obtained from various systems, from GNSS to ionosondes and topside sounders thanks to which NeQuick has been designed. The Global Ionosphere Maps (GIM) could be a robust and reliable data which suit for NeQuick model Ingestion. In this paper, the aim of this study is to show a preliminary assessment of the performance of the GIM-ingested NeQuick model apply in GPS Single Frequency Ionospheric Correction in China Region. GIM data are used to drive the NeQuick model for the effective ionization level which denoted by Az; While GPS observation data obtained from five stations in China region was used as metrics in this process. The results of the comparisons between GIM-ingested NeQuick and Klobuchar model are also analyzed; At last conclusions about the ionospheric correction performance of NeQuick in China region have been summed up.

articleTitle: Printed antenna with chip capacitance embedded for LTE/WWAN wireless USB dongle applications
abstract: A novel printed antenna is proposed, fabricated and tested for ultra-wideband LTE/GSM/UMTS WWAN wireless USB dongle attached to laptop computer. With a chip capacitance embedded in the design, a resonant mode at about 750 MHz is successfully excited to cover LTE700/GSM850/900 operating bands. The big radiating plate can generate two resonance frequencies to meet the bandwidth of GSM1800/1900/UMTS2100/LTE2300/2500. Owing to its simple structure low-profile and compact size, the proposed antenna can be easily integrated in the USB dongle with the other functional modules together. The measurement result achieves a good agreement with the simulation as well as good radiation characteristics, making it promising for wireless USB dongle mobile communication applications.

articleTitle: A study on EMC stress-strength interference model and EMC reliability
abstract: This paper proposed a new concept named EMC reliability to describe the capability of electromagnetic compatibility from the perspective of probability and statistics. Based on the model of EMC stress and EMC strength, an interference model between them is established to obtain the EMC reliability. The results show that this method could not only forecast the level of electromagnetic compatibility of the system effectively, but also provide a significant reference for EMC design and optimization.

articleTitle: Design of multi-beam antennas with Mu and Epsilon-Near-Zero metamaterials
abstract: Multi-beam antenna is a special device which is capable of radiating electromagnetic energies in different directions. In this paper, a Mu and Epsilon-Near-Zero (MENZ) metamaterial multi-beam antenna based on two-dimensional LC network is designed. The equivalent node voltage distribution matrix of this device is derived and its performance is simulated. We show that the radiation characteristic of the antenna is independent on the position of the current source as long as it is located in the MENZ region. The number of the beams and the radiation characteristic of the antenna can be flexibly adjusted by designing the shape and size of the MENZ region.

articleTitle: A novel focusing dielectric lens
abstract: For the shortcomings of the ordinary short focal length dielectric lens with large volume, the design of a new type of partition lens has been presented. And use simulation software to carry out a comparative analysis of this dielectric lens focusing properties with the traditional dielectric lens.

articleTitle: Application of the Genetic Algorithm to the design optimization of millimeter wave spaceborne frequency selective surface
abstract: We demonstrate a brand new class of band-pass frequency selective surface (FSS) for remote sensing applications. This satellite-bone device has an operating frequency at 118GHz, which is a typical frequency in O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> absorption line. Numerical method Periodic Method of Moment approach has been applied to determine the original geometrical structure and inter-unit spacing of FSS element, and the optimization technique based on the Genetic Algorithm empowered us to obtain the requisite spectral response and power conversion performance for TE and TM polarization. Comprising an ultra-thin gold layer and a SiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> dielectric layer, this complex GA-based periodic component exhibit a very low insertion loss (<;0.3dB) and high isolation (>;25dB) between closely spaced frequency channels at 45° incidence.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic leakage characteristics simulation of PD with the specific structure GIS disc insulator
abstract: Analysis on the transmission and leakage characteristics of PD (partial discharge) signal in GIS (Gas Insulated Switchgear) is of great significance for the study of signal propagation mechanism in GIS and circuit design for PD detection in engineering applications. Combined with the specific structure GIS disc insulator, the electromagnetic simulation software Ansoft HFSS is used to study the transmission and leakage characteristics of the electromagnetic wave in GIS through the establishment of different GIS models. The simulation results show that the frequency and amplitude of the leaked signals has something to do with the distance between two adjacent screws, the greater the distance, the lower the frequency of the leaked signals, the greater the radiation amplitude. Meanwhile, the transmission coefficient of PD signal in GIS is simulated by using dipole as the partial discharge signals and the result shows that the main leaked signal frequency band is 1.75GHZ-2.3GHZ with the minimum attenuation of -45DB, when the distance between the two adjacent screws equals to 15mm×55mm. The simulation results provide an important guiding significance for the design of partial discharge detection sensors and back-end circuit design in practical application.

articleTitle: Refractive error correction on radar target detection in evaporation duct
abstract: Geometrical Optics theory (GO) is effective to analyze and process high-frequency wave propagation in the case of short-wavelength or high-frequency limit. Using the ray tracing methods of GO, the ray paths of electromagnetic wave propagation are simulated in the standard atmosphere and the evaporation duct environment. The simulation results show that evaporation duct can significantly trap some radio rays to extend the propagation distance of EM wave and result in the appearance of radar blind zone. For radar target detection in duct environment, the ray tracing technique was used to calculate the error of propagation range, elevation angle and target height in the standard atmosphere and evaporation duct environment. Refractive error correction in evaporation duct has a beneficial effect on radar target detection.

articleTitle: A new planar electronically steerable passive array radiator antenna
abstract: A new planar electronic steering passive array radiator (ESPAR) antenna has been proposed for wireless communication mobile terminals in this paper. In order to achieve conical elevation pattern and compact size, a hexagon patch antenna shorted by two cylindrical metal pins to its ground plane is utilized. Compared with conventional switched array antennas, this array antenna has broadband and more compact planar structure. By controlling the status of RF switches, the presented antenna provides multiple radiation pattern. The array antenna's characteristics are analyzed by the full-wave electromagnetic simulator Ansoft HFSS v.10.0. Good characteristics have been achieved to demonstrate the performance improvement.

articleTitle: A composite circularly polarized dielectric complex waveguide slot antenna array with enhanced bandwidth
abstract: A novel Ka-band composite circularly polarized dielectric complex waveguide slot (CP-DCWS) antenna array is designed, fabricated and measured. The CP-DCWS antenna array is composed of a circular polarization grid, a slot microstrip line, a groove guide and feeding network. The slot microstrip line is formed by a metal clad dielectric substrate and slots etched in the metal.
