articleTitle: Laser scattering polarization characteristics of mist and painted target based on rotation angle
abstract: For the absence of laser polarization characteristics data, which can be used to distinguish between mist and painted metal target, then we have taken a test methods based on rotation angle of polarization of the incident laser, and measured the degree of linear polarization of thin mist and tanker samples, experimental result says: within the scope of the polarization angle of 45°, laser backscattering polarization characteristics have the ability to distinguish between mist and painted metal target samples. In order to verify this phenomenon, we changed frequency and pulse width parameters of the incident laser, then measured middle and high concentrations mist and painted armored vehicle samples. The verification results show that: under different frequency and pulse width of incident laser, with increasing the angle of incident laser polarization, the degree of laser backscattering polarization of mist decrease first and then increase, the minimum value of polarization show in 45°. But the degree of polarization of painted metal target samples do not change significantly, which are greater than middle and high concentration mist in the angle of 45°.

articleTitle: Plane wave scattering by a chiral-coating dielectric sphere
abstract: Using the spherical vector wave functions, an analytical solution to the scattering of a chiral-coated dielectric sphere with plane wave is presented. Applying the boundary conditions on each interface among the dielectric sphere, chiral medium and free space, the expansion coefficients for the internal and the scattered fields are determined. The influences of the chiral-coated spherical shell and the chiral parameter on radar cross section (RCS) are discussed numerically.

articleTitle: Scattering of electromagnetic pulse wave by spherical sand and dust particles
abstract: The generalized Lorentz-Mie formulas are used to study the scattering characteristics when a femtosecond pulse illuminates a spherical sand and dust particle. Efficiencies for extinction and scattering of pulse wave by sand and dust particles are calculated for different radii and pulse duration. The calculations show that even for pulses with a constant carrier wavelength and pulse-filling coefficient, the efficiencies for extinction and scattering differ very much between the carrier wave and the different pulses.

articleTitle: Study of reconfigurable high gain wide-angle antenna
abstract: A new structure like the Chinese character “t” for wide angle scan with high gain has been developed based on PIN diodes. The size of the structure and the reconfigurable mechanism are present in the details. The antennas from the structure satisfy the requirements on the maximum reflection coefficient of Γ ≤ 20 dB for ±60° and ±57. 5° from a broadside in E- and H- planes with a moderate gain of 4-7 dBi. The 2.4GHz antenna prototype is fabricated, tested experimentally and shows good performance to confirm the validity of the structure.

articleTitle: Sub-reflector extension shapes for reduced far-out side-lobes in offset Gregorian antennas
abstract: This paper presents a study of sub-reflector extension shapes to reduce the far-out side-lobes in offset Gregorian reflector configurations. It is shown that reflecting some of the energy from the extension back onto the main reflector instead of past it reduces the side-lobe past the main reflector as well as increase the aperture efficiency.

articleTitle: A tri-port attenuator for the test system of wireless keyboards
abstract: In this paper, a tri-port attenuator is proposed for the test system of wireless keyboards. The attenuation performance is achieved by using the couplers' isolating function ingeniously. The proposed attenuator can help to reduce crosstalk among the test systems and makes the systems have good uniformity. For the requirements of test system, the tri-port attenuator is designed and realized with -30dB attenuation at center frequency 2.45GHz. And its coupling coefficient is designed among -3~ -4dB for testers to monitor the received signal of the system conveniently.

articleTitle: A T-ψ decoupled scheme with C-N difference for a multiply connected eddy current problem
abstract: The aim of this paper is to present a new T-ψ finite element decoupled scheme with Crank-Nicholson difference format for time-dependent eddy current problem, which avoids solving a saddle-point equations system and is more economical than the traditional scheme. The holes of multiply connected conductors are stemmed by making "cuts" and jumps of the function value ψ across the "cuts" are enforced. The construction of the finite element space with discontinuities at the "cuts" are given. The superior performance of the decoupled scheme is demonstrated by numerical experiment of the benchmark problem-TEAM Workshop Problem 7.

articleTitle: Sensitiveness of cloaking performance on moderate material parameter violation
abstract: A coordinate transformation approach dictates inhomogeneous and anisotropic medium in cloaks' design. In this paper, the sensitiveness of different cloaking schemes based approximate cloaks, in which the EM parameters are limited to a range more plausible to realize, is investigated. When devising the cloak using dispersive lossy metamaterials, the unavoidable deviation in material parameters degraded the cloak's performance significantly, especially in terms of bandwidth. Numerical experiments show that the imperfect cloak under moderate compression presents low anisotropy and is a candidate scheme more insusceptible to moderate changes in EM parameters.

articleTitle: Approximate solution for vertically polarized VLF/LF waves in lower ionosphere
abstract: The oblique reflection of VLF/LF radio waves from lower ionosphere is considered. The profile of the effective conductivity is considered as an exponential one. An approximation formula is presented for calculating the reflection coefficient of vertically polarized waves in the conduction of isotropic. The simulating results agree well with the measurements.

articleTitle: Three unit cell CRLH-TL based Zeroth order resonance antenna
abstract: In this paper a Zeroth order resonance antenna based on CRLH-TL technique is proposed. To achieve a compact size antenna utilizes the ZOR phenomenon and its reactive parameters determine the resonant frequency. It consists of three top patches and the meander lines are connected to the rectangular patch. Here the meander lines acts as an inductor and the rectangular patch as a virtual ground capacitor. The proposed antenna has the benefit of compact size and easy to fabricate. The efficiency of 77% and gain of 5.445 dBi and operates at 3.1049GHz.

articleTitle: Wide-band circularly polarized antenna for dual-band GPS receiver
abstract: In this letter, the design of a wide-band circularly polarized microstrip antenna with gain of more than 8dB is introduced. This antenna is designed for the global positioning satellite operations at 1227 MHz(L<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>) and 1575 MHz(L<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sub>). It has an advantage of a much wider band in both VSWR and 3dB axial-ratio compared with single-feed GPS antennas. Details of design, simulated results of this GPS antenna are presented and discussed. The results confirm the validity of this design which meet the requirement of GPS application.

articleTitle: Miniaturized ultrawideband multifunction vehicular antenna for terrestrial and satellite communications
abstract: This paper presents a new design of miniaturized integrated multifunction antenna for all terrestrial services over 0.7–7.0 GHz and satellite services over 1.1–2.4 GHz, covering essentially all radio technologies implemented now or on the drawing board for mobile communications. It has the advantages of small size, good form-factor, low cost, and aesthetic appeal.

articleTitle: A new implementation of Asymptotic Waveform Evaluation for fast frequency analysis
abstract: A pseudo-spectral method is adopted instead of conventionally finding the derivative formulations before discretization in Asymptotic Waveform Evaluation (AWE) procedure. The complexity of Method of Moments(MOM) conjunction with this new implementation is generally much less than the conventional one. Furthermore, this pseudo-spectral method does not require finding the derivative of green functions with respect to frequency so that AWEcan be applied to the hybrid finite element - boundary integral - multilevel fast multipole algorithm (FE-BI-MLFMA).

articleTitle: The correction of mutual coupling and the amplitude and phase error based on digital beamforming receiving antenna
abstract: By measuring the GPS antenna pattern, based on the minimum variance distortionless response adaptive beamforming principle, An easy method to suppress the mutual coupling between array antenna elements and the amplitude and phase errors was presented in this paper and the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm was validated in a four-element linear equispaced array and circular array and simulation results show the performance of this method.

articleTitle: Analysis EM characteristics of tiny periodic structure with FDTD method
abstract: In the military and civil areas, the electromagnetic characteristics of tiny periodic structure have aroused people attention. In this paper, the reflection and transmission coefficients of inerratic metal periodic structure are analyzed by the Finite-Difference Time-Domain (FDTD) Method. The influence of incident wave angle, diameter of metal wire, size of periodic structure is considered. Numerical example indicated that FDTD is an effective tool to study electromagnetic characteristics of tiny periodic structure.

articleTitle: Modeling high-altitude Na atom behavior in ionospheric chemical reaction system
abstract: Observations show that Na atom can sporadically occur at higher altitude above the region within 80-105 km where they normally inhabit. The formation mechanism of this high-altitude sporadic Na layer is not clear at present. In this study, based on a time-resolved ionospheric gas-phase chemical reaction model, we have surveyed the behaviour of high-altitude Na atoms under the injection of meteoroids or occurrence of sporadic E layer, to explore the formation process of high-altitude sporadic Na layer.

articleTitle: Research on ionosphere drift velocity based on digisonde observation
abstract: In this paper, a simply method was introduced to be calculated drift velocity of the ionosphere by analysis the frequency shift and phase change of the receiving signals from digisonde. By using data was observed with TR169 station at Tromso (E19.2°, N69.6°) and JI91J station at Jicamarca (W76.8°, S12.0°) in 2010, the ionosphere drift velocity were calculated and analyzed. Meanwhile, an analysis of kp index on February 2010 shows that the change of kp index influence on the ionosphere drift velocity at high-latitude is more significant than at low-latitude. Finally, a statistical analysis of the drift velocities at this two places show that the component of the drift velocity is mainly horizontal eastward. The daily average velocity at Tromso is nearly to Jicamarca and the average speed rates are obviously greater than Jicamarca, which may be caused by the more complex environments, it also results more difficulties for calculating the velocity at high-latitude.

articleTitle: Design of wideband CPW-Fed circularly polarized slot antenna
abstract: This paper presents a novel compact wideband CPW-fed circularly polarized (CP) printed slot antenna. The proposed antenna features an irregular slot and a tapered tuning stub protruded into the slot from the signal strip of the CPW. Wideband CP operation is achieved by changing the shapes of the slot. The simulated bandwidths of 3-dB axial ratio (AR) and 10-dB return loss are respectively around 91% (1.9 GHz-6 GHz) and 82% (2.7 GHz-6.4GHz) with the center frequency of 4.5GHz. The CP bandwidth of this antenna is 73% (from 2.7 GHz to 6 GHz). The measured gain is more than 3.8dBi over the CP bandwidth. Overall antenna size is 0.9λ×0.9λ with the thickness of 1mm, relative to the center frequency of 4.5 GHz.

articleTitle: Incoherent scatter spectra of plasma with Bump-on-tail distribution
abstract: During artificial ionospheric modification and convective electric field, plasma is in an iopsided state, and the velocity distribution of particles is non-Maxwellian. Application of the empirical Bump-on-tail distribution of electrons in incoherent scatter spectra of plasma is studied in this paper. Features of the distribution function are discussed. With Bump-on-tail distribution function, numerical simulations of incoherent scatter spectra are given. The conclusion is that the Bump-on-tail distribution function is suitable to analysis some exceptional incoherent scatter spectra.

articleTitle: Design of a new type of ultra wideband planar antenna
abstract: In view of a particular GIS structure, a new type of planar antenna with extremely wide bandwidth is introduced. Due to the analysis of the relationship between antenna impedance and bandwidth, the investigated antenna bandwidth is broadened. The influence of dimension on antenna VSWR is optimized by using the simulation software Ansoft HFSS. Then, an antenna prototype is fabricated and measured. The impedance bandwidth from 1.29 GHz to 5.1 GHz is achieved at VSWR≤2.5 with dimensions of 72mm×44mm, which has the ultra wideband performance. The antenna has the characteristic of simple structure, small size, wideband, easy to make, low cost of manufacture, and can be used for UHF partial discharge in the special structure of GIS.

articleTitle: A novel multi-band antenna for WLAN and WiMAX applications
abstract: A novel compact antenna with four-band operation is proposed for WLAN/WiMAX applications. The multi-band performance is obtained through the parasitic inverted U-shaped element, the defected ground plane and an inverted L-shaped slot in the signal strip line, all of which printed on the substrate with a single metallic layer. To compact the antenna size and overcome the high impedance problem, the signal strip line is designed to be located at the left of the rectangular ground plane. Such structure can cause meandering of the surface current paths, which lead to lower the resonant frequency of the antenna, corresponding to a reduced antenna size. Furthermore, the design capability of multi-band operation has also been explained in the later part of the study.

articleTitle: Analysis of electromagnetic characteristics of antenna arrays based on the characteristic basis function method
abstract: The characteristic basis function method (CBFM) is used to analyze the electromagnetic characteristics of antenna arrays in this paper. The original antenna arrays are divided into a number of subdomains and high-level basis functions are constructed for each subdomain through their couplings, the resulting matrix can be largely reduced. The characteristic basis function method not only has high accuracy and computing time is greatly reduced. The numerical results are given to illustrate that the method is accurate and efficient.

articleTitle: Small-slope approximation for electromagnetic wave scattering at the dielectric rough sea surface
abstract: In this paper, the bistatic coefficient of the first-order and the second-order small slope approximation is derived for the dielectric rough surface. Based on the spectral model of Elfouhaily, the scattering coefficient of rough surface is calculated, and the theoretical results are compared between the polarization VV and the polarization HH, the dependence of the backscattering coefficient on the wind speed and the dielectric constant. The results showed that theoretical results are consistent with experimental data. In the case of the backscattering, the result calculated by the small slope approximation is accuracy and the second-order makes the results more accuracy.

articleTitle: Study on morphological characteristics of ionosphere scintillation in the high-latitude region
abstract: Based on the weak scattering theory and assumed that the behaviour of ionospheric plasma turbulence influences on the VHF signals can be simulated by a series of phase changing diffraction screen models. In this article, by using the model, the formulas of the intensity scintillation index and the phase variance of the signal are derived and discussed. Meanwhile, the variational characteristics of the above parameters were analyzed with different seasonal, solar activity, and geomagnetic index. Finally, the intensity scintillation index changes with diurnal and seasonal is inversed successfully. The research shows that the week scattering phase model can satisfactorily describe the characteristics of the scintillation in the high-latitude ionosphere.

articleTitle: The influence of meteoric smoke particle attributions on polar mesospheric clouds formation
abstract: It is known that the formation of polar mesospheric clouds (PMCs) is correlated with temperature, concentration and desublimation nuclei of water vapor. The primary candidate of these nuclei is believed to be meteoric smoke particles. In this study, we have surveyed the influence of meteoric smoke particle attributions on polar mesospheric ice clouds formation. It is found that the large smoke particles with radium of 2–3 nm will dominate the nucleation of water vapor.

articleTitle: The circuit-level simulation of continuous Wave Doppler Fuze detector based on ADS
abstract: Simulation of fuze detector using conventional simulation softwares requires tremendous complicated theoretical calculations. It also can't analyze the impact caused by the nonlinear of the analog devices. A circuit-level simulation method is proposed in this paper to solve this problem, based on the implementation of continuous wave Doppler fuze detector on ADS simulation platform. Continuous Wave Doppler Fuze detector model is built on the ADS platform by using components and Microstrip Line as the same as real circuit and optimizing the analog components parameters by impedance matching. This model launches a Continuous wave signal which has the frequency between 3.36GHz and 3.5GHz, and generates an IF signal of a magnitude between 150mv to 200mv. The results show that this scheme is reasonable and feasible.

articleTitle: Optoelectronic image process the scaling ratios between the light scattering characteristic and geometric dimensions of the target
abstract: The experimental measurement and image processing methods are combined to study the light scattering characteristic from the target, principle of the scaling ratio between the light scattering characteristic and the geometric dimension of the target is presented in this paper. The solar simulator is utilized as a light source which incidence the target with rough surface. The original experimental images must be measured by light receiver and data gathering system. Some image algorithms are be designed to process these experimental data. As a researching example, the imaging light scattering characteristic of two kinds of bigger and smaller simple targets include clubs, cylinders are discussed in detail. The image processed results are shown the scale ratio of the light scattering from target is proportional to its dimensional square. The important of our works is that the scaling rations of the light scattering characteristic can be used to make known the illumination of the whole dimensional detected target, which are useful for further study the complex target such as civilian industries, national defence, air and aero fields.

articleTitle: Performance appraisal of anti-interference technology with adaptive nulling antenna based on SINR of array output
abstract: We proposes an interference mathematical model of LMS algorithm beam forming after analyzing LMS using matrix theory, and we also build another mathematical model of output SINR (Signal to Interference and Noise Ratio) by assuming the signal and interference are unrelated. Then, based on these models, we further analyze the anti-noise performance of LMS algorithm when there are no inference signals, while when there are interference signals we make the conclusion that the algorithm affects the interference totally different under different degree of interference. At last, we test and verify our analysis using mathematical emulation, and make the performance appraisal of anti-interference technology with adaptive nulling antenna.

articleTitle: Scattering by two concentric ferrite anisotropic spheres
abstract: Based on spherical vector wave functions(SVWFs) in ferrite anisotropic medium, and the first, second spherical Bessel functions satisfying the same differential equation and recursive formula, the electromagnetic fields in two concentric ferrite anisotropic spheres, and free space can be expressed in terms of SVWFs in anisotropic ferrite medium, and isotropic medium. Applying the continue boundary conditions of electromagnetic fields in the interface of the ferrite anisotropic spherical shell, the coefficients of electromagnetic fields in terms of SVWFs in ferrite anisotropic medium in two concentric ferrite anisotropic spheres and scattering fields in free space are derived. Numerical results for the very general ferrite dielectric media are obtained and those in a special case are compared between the present method and the Method of Moments (MoM) speeded up with the Conjugate-Gradient Fast-Fourier-Transform (CG-FFT) approach. The present method can be probably used in antenna and radiowave propagation, etc.

articleTitle: Time-domain physical optics method for the analysis of wide-band EM scattering from two dimensional conducting rough surface
abstract: In this paper, we extend the application of time-domain physical optics (TDPO) method to investigate electromagnetic (EM) scattering from two dimensional perfectly electrically conducting (PEC) rough surface in time domain. The scheme requires relatively small amounts of computer memory and CPU time, as well as has advantage over the Kirchhoff Approximation (KA) method in obtaining transient response of rough surface. The 2D Gaussian randomly rough surface is generated by Monte Carlo method and divided into small triangle facets though the meshing preprocess. The accuracy of TDPO method is validated by comparing the analytical results with those obtained by the KA method in the backward and specular direction. The transient response and its frequency distribution of radar cross section (RCS) from rough surface are given, respectively. Finally, the simulations of electromagnetic scattering from PEC rough surface are carried out to analyze the variation of RCS with correlation length (l) and root mean square height (σ).

articleTitle: Modelling and analysis of electromagnetic interferences for a 32-bit digital signal controller
abstract: This paper presents the modelling and analysis of electromagnetic interferences (EMI) for a 32-bit digital signal controller (DSC) that enables uncompromising performance and real-time control applications for high electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) requirement. The EMI behaviour model of the DSC for conducted emission, built upon the package and chip dies, is used to predict the EM emissions of the chip and printed circuit board (PCB) levels. The characterization of EMI has been analyzed by circuital simulations and conducted emission measurements according to the EMC model. It is successfully demonstrated that the simulated results are consistent with the predictions generated by using the proposed model. And the DSCs chip model, simulation and measurement of the EMI are necessary for the analysis, prediction, and compatibility of the PCB and systems design.

articleTitle: Optimization and design of a wideband vertically stacked Yagi-Uda antenna array with a wide azimuth HPBW
abstract: A vertically stacked Yagi-Uda antenna array with X-shape driven dipoles for the long range Meteor Burst Communication(MBC) at the VHF is presented using differential evolution algorithm (DE). In order to illustrate the capabilities of the method, a 3-element Yagi-Uda antenna array is given. The measured and simulated impedance bandwidth of VSWR<;1.4 reaches 22% and some solved methods are proposed to cope with the demand from wide azimuth HPBW. The results show that the simulated antenna gain across the operating frequency band is 8.1~8.3dB and the HPBW in the azimuth plane is above 90°.

articleTitle: Mutual coupling calibration for electromagnetic vector sensor array
abstract: In superresolution direction-fingding, mutual coupling error among electromagnetic vector sensor's six component-antennas could degrade system performance obviously, so effective calibration is needed. At first, the cause for error is analyzed and a model of array mutual coupling error is established. Then matrix was transformed according to the special structure of error matrix and reduced the parameters' dimensions and the amount of calculation. At last, the simulation results demonstrated that this approach is correct and effective.

articleTitle: Research on HTc rf SQUID magnetic sensor calibration
abstract: With advantages of high sensitivity, small size, and easy integration, HTc rf SQUID magnetic sensor is important means of weak magnetic signal detection and reception including bio-magnetic measurements, nondestructive testing, and geophysical exploration. To improve the measurement accuracy, calibration of HTc rf SQUID sensors is necessary. Due to the different principles, the calibration method of HTc rf SQUID magnetic sensor is not the same as that of the other conventional magnetic sensors. Relying on laboratory conditions, we conduct the HTc SQUID magnetic sensor calibration and study the calibration method suitable to the HTc rf SQUID magnetic sensor.

articleTitle: A fast visualized computation method for LRCS
abstract: A method for computing LRCS of a complex rough surface object is given. It is based on the application of color-flagged modelling method and the five-parameter semi empirical statistical expression of BRDF theory. Two examples are discussed to show the validity and effectiveness of the method in laser scattering characteristics analysis and simulation.

articleTitle: Design of the Continuous Transverse Stub array
abstract: In this paper, a new type of antenna arrays, that is, a twelve-element CTS antenna array is discribed. The Continuous Transverse Stub (CTS) array represents a unique class of array antenna that exploits the low-loss, low-dispersion, dimensional robustness, and design flexibility of an open parallel-plate structure as both its transmission-line and radiator basis. The design of the CTS array was optimized through simulation using Ansoft high frequency structure simulator (HFSS). It could be adapted for base station applications in wireless communtions, for satellite communication systems.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic analysis in the ship RCS plastics design
abstract: In this paper, setting out from typical structures — metal plate, and discussing the relation of RCS with incident angle, frequency of radar wave, and geometry of metal plate, the formula, which characterizes the RCS of the plate with inclined angle, has been derived by physical optics theory. Through the formula, the optimal inclined angle can be determined at single frequency and multiple frequencies. Also, an example is presented to illustrate how to make a compromised design according to formulas considering stealthy of the ship and volume of the cabin. The results are significant to the stealthy design of ship.

articleTitle: Near field scattering measurement based on ISAR imaging technique
abstract: In this paper, a method of near field scattering measurement based on ISAR imaging technique is introduced. Put the target on a turntable for near field Inverse Synthetic Aperture Radar (ISAR) imaging, and get the position and amplitude information of scattering center from the image, then predict its far field Radar Cross Section (RCS). The results of computer simulation show that the RCS obtained by this method agree very well with the theoretical RCS value.

articleTitle: A design of triple-band planar inverted-F antenna for mobile communication
abstract: With the increase of people's needs in the field of mobile communications, the requirements of the mobile terminal are also getting higher and higher. The mobile phone antenna as an important component of the wireless communications, we should consider the multi-band and multifunction characteristics in the design. On the basis of above considerations, we designed a new tri-band (GSM/DCS/ISM) planar inverted F-type mobile phone antenna to meet the needs of applications such as multimode phone, Wifi or Bluetooth. We can achieve the required performance of the antenna by adjusting the length of the gap between the slots and the feed point location, and the two U-shaped slots can produce a tri-band antenna. When the VSWR<;2.5, GSM900, DCS1800 and ISM1800 are all included in the working frequency band. By using software of HFSS, we can simulate the model and optimize the antenna structure to achieve the required frequency and radio characteristics.

articleTitle: Fast EMP response calculation of dipole antennas based on equivalent circuit
abstract: An approach to fast calculate electromagnetic Pulse (EMP) response with equivalent circuit is proposed. Based on the equivalence concept of EMP radiation source and dipole antennas, the response at receiving antenna port is calculated efficiently with a simple circuit composed of pulse voltage source and lumped elements. Two cases of an example are taken to evaluate the validity of the calculation method. Comparing with the full wave simulation results, the equivalent calculation method can speed up the evaluation of EMP response and can be easily used in circuit software packages.

articleTitle: The MLFMA basis method for RCS calculation of discontinuous character objects
abstract: A new numerical method called the half multilevel fast multipole algorithm basis method (MLFMABM) for highly efficient and accurate Radar Cross Section (RCS) calculations of complex discontinuous characters is presented. The proposed method is used to estimate the RCS of a multi-discontinuous character plate based on a single-discontinuous character plate and its corresponding plate with no discontinuous character. It is shown that MLFMABM can achieve high efficiency and precision.

articleTitle: The calculation methods of coupling coefficient between resonators
abstract: Three calculation formulas are derived based on the definition of coupling coefficient by three methods, namely, adding electric and magnetic wall method, setting the imaginary part of resistance to zero and S parameter method. The hairpin coupling microstrip resonator module is established and calculation methods is given by using microwave simulation software. The coupling coefficient is calculated and simulation results are obtained under the circumstance of variable interval between resonators. Three calculation results are shown. Firstly, the method of adding electric and magnetic wall is an accurate method in calculating the coupling coefficient between resonators, but it is only suitable for symmetrical structure. Secondly, the method of circuit resistant calculation is an accurate method in engineering, but the calculation of loaded Q is more complicated. Thirdly, S parameter method uses microwave simulation software to obtain the amplitude and phase curve of transformation parameter S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">21</sub>, it doesn't has much requirement on the resonator structure, and it is suitable for computer simulation and engineering design.

articleTitle: Ionosphere TEC prediction based on Chaos
abstract: This paper proved the chaotic property of ionosphere total electron content (TEC) by using the data in 1997 and 2001 at Wuhan station, based on Chaos theory. The time delay was calculated by using mutual information method, the best embedding dimension was calculated by using G-P method and the largest Lyapunov exponent was calculated by using small data method. Based upon this, it constructed the forecasting network with an advanced time of one or twenty-four hours by means of BP Neural Network and using the data of 1998 and 2002 to test the network. Analysis of the forecasting error indicates that one hour ahead prediction network which can reach high accuracy is quite suitable for quasi real-time prediction of ionosphere TEC over this region, twenty-four hours ahead prediction can controlled the relative error to be about 10%. The average absolute error is about 1.6256TECU during solar minimum, far less than 6.4575 TECU predicted during solar maximum. The forecasting error is relative high when magnetic storm happens on the morning, noon and sunset.

articleTitle: Wideband CRLH-transmission line bandstop filter
abstract: A new compact broadband bandstop filter using composite right/left handed transmission line (CRLH-TL) is presented. The filter is designed based on a signal interference mechanism. The CRLH-TL is used to substitute the three-quarter-wavelength transmission line, thus the total size is largely reduced. A meandered slotline is etched on the ground plane below the interdigital capacitor to improve the upper passband performance. A bandstop filter with about 70% fractional bandwidth (FBW) at 3 GHz has been designed and fabricated. The size of the fabricated filter is 0.23 λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">g</inf> × 0.084 λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">g</inf>.

articleTitle: General expressions of propagation vector of electromagnetic wave for lossless anisotropic media
abstract: Three general representations of the eign-propagating vectors are presented for the lossless anisotropic medium, respectively. When the lossless medium is uniaxial crystal, the phase velocities and the corresponding eign-propagating vectors are entirely agreement with what in the literatures, when the medium is an isotropic one, the phase velocities and the corresponding eign-propagating vectors are also agreement with what in the literatures in theory. The validity of the results is demonstrated. The representations of these eign-propagating vectors are not confined by the permittivity tensor.

articleTitle: Radiation and scattering of the microstrip antenna with slotted ground plane
abstract: Radiation and scattering properties are two important factors of the antenna, especially for the antenna used in military system. In this paper, the radiation and scattering properties of a modified microstrip antenna with slots in the ground plane is studied. The backscattering and bi-static scattering properties both in-band and out-band of the antenna are analyzed. The results of this antenna are compared with those of the commonly used microstrip antenna. It is found that although the radiation property is slight degraded, the scattering property of the microstrip antenna with slotted ground plane is much better than that of the commonly used antenna. The results of this paper provide a possible way of designing microstrip antenna with low scattering properties.

articleTitle: Performance analysis of the ultrawideband impulse radar pulses and echoes distributed over fiber
abstract: In this paper, a system model of UWB radar distributed over optical fiber is proposed. The bidirectional transmission performance of UWB pulses and echoes over optical fiber is analyzed. The theoretical simulation results demonstrate that 80km distribution distance can be achieved with the two modulation schemes of Optical Carrier Suppression and Single SideBand to keep the echo SNR larger than 10dB, when the fiber dispersion is fully compensated with dispersion compensation fiber (DCF).

articleTitle: Curvature limitation in local planar approximation of radome
abstract: To discover the applicable curvature range of local planar approximation in high frequency radome analysis approaches, ray tracing (RT) method and aperture integration-surface integration (AI-SI) method are employed to calculation the power transmittance of the radomes with a limited number of well-controlled dielectric wall curvature perturbations. By comparison of the two techniques with method of moments (MoM), it is demonstrated that the curvature radius should not be less than five wavelengths in this approximation.

articleTitle: On the analysis of the load response of transmission line network based on electromagnetic topology-COG
abstract: This paper presents a method in analysing of the induced voltages in transmission line networks, which uses electromagnetic topology based on COG for simplifying the complexity of the wirings, and the hybrid BLT-FDTD method proposed for calculation of the network contains non-uniform lines. Simulation is performed for a typical cables network. The results are compared with those under complete interaction sequence diagram showing the accuracy and efficiency of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Calibration of biconical antennas on a small ground plane
abstract: A new way is proposed, and verified by experiment, to measure the free-space antenna factor (Fafs) of biconical antenna over 30 MHz to 300 MHz, by the standard antenna method. The antennas were horizontally polarized above a small (12 m wide) open area test site (OATS). The usual method of calibrating EMC antennas is to place two antennas at a given separation in a horizontal plane. Biconical antennas have a uniform H-plane pattern, making it possible to stack the antennas in a vertical plane. The Fafs measured with the new method is in close agreement (difference less than 0.6 dB) to that with the vertically polarized method from the draft IEC international standard CISPR 16-1-6. Because the antennas are stacked vertically, a smaller ground plane can be used. Because the antennas are horizontally polarized, the vertically routed cable is orthogonal to the antenna so the interaction of cable and antenna is minimized.

articleTitle: Seasonal results of aspect sensitivity from an MF radar over Kunming (25.6°N, 103.8°E), China
abstract: The physical shapes and causes of these partial reflection scatterers for MF radar is, as yet, an unsolved question. The aspect sensitivity parameterized by a quantity θ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">S</sub> is defined often as the rate of decrease of power as a function of angle. Small values of θ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">S</sub> imply the existence of specular scatterers. The seasonal results of aspect sensitivity from Kunming MF radar have been studied based on the first 12 months data, which shows a clear seasonal dependence with the bigger values in winter and the smaller values in summer. Aspect sensitivity also presents an evident variation in height, increasing between 80 and 90 km while decreasing from 90 to 100 km. Turbulence velocity measured during the same period supports the proposal that turbulences play an important role in causing specular scatterers which produces aspect sensitivity in D-region for MF radar.

articleTitle: Collision absorption and resonance absorption of electromagnetic waves by array plasma
abstract: This article described the experiment on the absorption of 1-18GHz electromagnetic (EM) waves by array plasma which was produced by many standard commercial fluorescent lamps placed directly against each other in two rows. Weak reflection and strong absorption were observed. Predictive peak electron density and collision frequency were discussed and compared with measurement. The results indicated that the single-pass collision absorption reached the maximum of about 10dB, when incident frequency approached to collision frequency. Resonance absorption took place in the case of plasma properties varying along electric field of incident wave, when the incident frequency approached to the peak plasma frequency.

articleTitle: The topside EMC pre-design method for ship platform
abstract: This paper presents a “top-down” pre-design method of electromagnetic compatibility for ship platform. Through constructing the energy-transfer model and relating matrix of the being interfered systems at the stage of concept-design of new ship, we can use numerical electromagnetic simulation, behavioral model, simulated testing, and data statistics method to evaluate the whole-all electromagnetic status, complete index assignment and optimization design of sensitive equipments and systems. The good ship platform EMC performance can be achieved by evaluating EMC performance, assigning the EMC indexes quantificationally. Additionally, the system EMC performance can be analyzed along with the change of subsystem or equipments EMC indexes, and the subsystem or equipments parameters can be adjusted to meet the system EMC requirements as well. And following these steps, we can control electromagnetic status for the all and the one of different ship platforms and potential EMC problems can be exposed at the stage of pre-design and resolved before the design is finalized.

articleTitle: Radiation characteristics of leaky cables with periodic slots under snow environment
abstract: The leaky cables, such as the leaky coaxial cable and leaky circular waveguide, are capable of distributing much smoother radio wave coverage than the discrete antenna system. However, when the leaky cables are used in the urban mass transit, they might be influenced by the extremely bad weather, especially for the low temperature and accumulated snow. In this paper, the influences of snow coverage with different volumetric wetness and different temperature on the near field distributions and the radiation characteristics of the leaky coaxial cable and leaky circular waveguide are simulated and analyzed. It is valuable to the design of the leaky cables.

articleTitle: Signal attenuation time series prediction method based on the chaos algorithm
abstract: Signal distortion will appear and a series of attenuation time series will also be produced due to the interaction between the radio wave signal and the ionospheric irregularities when radio wave propagates through it. In this article, based on the traditional chaotic time series prediction and the characteristic of the attenuation time series of the ionosphere, the traditional method for prediction the chaotic time series is modified, analyzed, and a more suitable method is given. Final, by using the modified prediction method, a set of attenuate amplitude time series of radio wave signals which propagates through the ionosphere were predicted, and the prediction accuracy is also analyzed. The research shows that the modified prediction method is suitable to predict the short-term time series.

articleTitle: Further comparison of basic MUF prediction based on different ionosphere models during medium epoch of the solar activity
abstract: As an extended research, basic MUF of nine circuits in China eastern region during medium epoch of the solar activity was collected, which azimuth ranges from 23.9 ° to 357.9°, and distance from 519.5 km to 2118.4 km. Then, basic MUF theoretical prediction based on ITU-R reference ionospheric model and China reference ionospheric model are compared. The results show that: basic MUF predicted result based on China reference ionospheric model is better than that based on ITU-R reference ionospheric model in China region. It is agreeable to the conclusion during minimum epoch of the solar activity.

articleTitle: Symmetric/asymmetric H-plane horn fed offset parabolic reflector antenna with switchable pencil/fan-beam radiation characteristics
abstract: This paper presents a modified offset parabolic reflector antenna design with easily switchable pencil/fan-beam radiation patterns for X-band tracking, scanning and surveillance microwave radar systems. The modified offset parabolic reflector antenna, combined with an array of flat aluminum plates at the bottom, is fed through symmetric/asymmetric H-plane feed horn antennas. An effective measured pencil-beam/fan-beam switching performance has been achieved as a result of setting the flares of the H-plane feed horn antenna symmetrically and asymmetrically, without making any changes in the geometry of the offset parabolic reflector antenna.

articleTitle: Towards super-resolution microwave imaging: General framework
abstract: Over past decades, there are growing intensive interests of achieving imaging resolution beyond that mainly constrained to system bandwidth, for example, the so-called Rayleigh diffraction limit. Three directions of research aiming to beat this limit are strongly advocated, i.e., (1) to exploit the evanescent components capturing the subtle details of the electromagnetic field at the immediate proximity of the object to be probed; (2) to develop the imaging algorithm of treating the specific type of imaged object, namely, the sparse object; (3) to design the precise instrument dedicated to create constructive subtle inference. This paper proposed a general framework of super-resolution imaging algorithm, which has the advantages that (a) of highly efficient and can be used for real-time imaging, (b) the sub-wavelength reconstruction, roughly, the resolution can be improved to be the factor of three times compared with the traditional imaging approaches. The key ingredient of proposed methodology is to construct an off-line filter, whose basic function is to produce so-called super-oscillation waves, leading to a sub-wavelength focus of prescribed size and shape in a field of view. Numerical and experimental results have demonstrated the state-of-art performance of the proposed approach, and open a new promising door to real-time super-resolution imaging, regarding computational complexity and imaging resolution.

articleTitle: Spectrum monitoring based on USRP2 receiver
abstract: The spectrum monitoring has gained new aspects with the development of cognitive radio and dynamic spectrum access technology. It is also one of the most challenging issues in spectrum management. In this paper, a spectrum monitoring technique using software defined radio is proposed. A prototype setup based on USRP2 with WBX and MATLAB/Simulink is designed and implemented. The spectrum of 50-2200 MHz band was measured. The results show that the prototype setup is capable of detecting the main radio signals within these bands, and spectrum in FM frequency band, digital TV band, GSM and 3G band can be observed.

articleTitle: A novel broadband dual-band dual circular polarization stacked microstrip antenna
abstract: This paper presents a novel design of a dual-band dual circular polarization stacked microstrip antenna. Multilayer structure and four gap-coupled probe feeds are employed. The simulated results indicate that the antenna has a good performance of return loss, radiation pattern and wide-range axial ratio bandwidth. The antenna can cover GPS and part of CNSS frequency band with good performance.

articleTitle: The long-term trend variation of ionospheric parameter's difference at 43.8°N station of China
abstract: The difference of the month median value at two typical equilatitudinal mid-latitude stations Urumchi (43.8°N, 87.6°E) and Changchun (43.83°N, 125.2°E), China are used to study the ionpsheric long-term trend. The main results are: (1) there is no obvious long-term trend for ΔfoE. This point is different from Jarvis (2008), who use the data from the station near the boundary between the ocean and continent. (2) there are positive (increasing) trend in daytime and little negative trend in night for ΔfoF2, which is maybe related to the difference of meridional wind. There are notable seasonal variations: the negative trend with minimum in summer, positive trend with maximum in equinox. (3) The ΔhmF2 show negative trend in all month and local time. There is a minimum at noon in June and larger value in other seasons. The trend of ΔhmF2 is maybe related to the spatial variability in the trend of thermosphere.

articleTitle: Fast calculation of RCS over a broad frequency band using FDM and AWE technique
abstract: The fast dipole method (FDM) in conjunction with the asymptotic waveform evaluation (AWE) technique is presented for fast calculation of radar cross section (RCS) from arbitrarily shaped perfect electric conductor targets over a broad frequency band. The FDM, which is based on the equivalent dipole-moment (EDM) method, is employed to reduce impedance matrix storage and accelerate the matrix-vector multiplications in the solutions of the Taylor coefficients. The application of AWE technique enables fast frequency sweep analysis. The numerical results show that this method greatly increased the computational efficiency without losing accuracy conditions compared with the traditional method of moments (MoM) combined with AWE technique.

articleTitle: Laser narrow pulse target transient response simulation model
abstract: Research with the foreign target transient response development, calculation method of laser narrow pulse transient response is put forward. Based on laser narrow pulse transient response theory, it is simulated by using mathematical model to get the transient responses of several typical ground and low-altitude targets after analyzing, data analysis indicates that this feature can be directly used for target classification, having large differences in shape and size, confirmed the feasibility of this method can provide data support and technical support for further identification of the target classification.

articleTitle: Pure time domain planar near field scattering measurements
abstract: Time domain planar near field scattering measurements can obtain wideband scattering data in one measurement. Time domain measuring method is based on plane wave spectrum formulas. This paper concerns simulation of time domain planar near field scattering measurements in time domain. The near-field scattering measurement data are transformed to far-field scattering data such as Radar Cross Section (RCS). The formulas of this method, derivation of the formulas, the simulation method, correction factor in time domain transformation, the simulation results and analysis are presented in this paper.

articleTitle: Mutual coupling isolating experiment for the plate end-fire antenna array
abstract: This paper focuses on decoupling in plate end-fire antenna array. The far field pattern distortions of array caused by mutual coupling were analysed. Then, the mutual coupling isolating experiments were carried out. After optimization of the isolating structure, an appropriate far field performance of linear array was achieved, which distortion rate had declined from 21.73% to 15.50%.

articleTitle: Simulation of ionospheric effects on SAR imaging with noise at P-band
abstract: In the past, most of the spaceborne synthetic aperture radars (SAR) operating at C-band or higher frequencies, and the ionospheric effects are negligible in these bands. Recently, the use of lower frequencies for measuring the foliage and ground penetration has been an increasing interest. However, the ionosphere is a highly dispersive medium, and can cause group delay and pulse broadening when the carrier frequency is low, such as P-band. Thus the range resolution in SAR imaging is degraded due to the ionospheric effects. And the irregularity of the ionosphere also can reduce the azimuthal resolution. Furthermore, the spaceborne SAR receiver would generate noise, which affects the quality of the echoes so as to SAR imaging. This paper presents both the analytical study and numerical simulation to investigate the ionospheric effects on SAR imaging with Gaussian white noise at P-band.

articleTitle: A far-field measurement system for the multichannel phased arrays antenna
abstract: In order to accomplish measurement of an multichannel phased arrays antenna transmit and receive characteristic quickly and automatically, this paper gives the design of an far-field antenna auto test system based on LAN bus and hardware trigger signal. By studying the integrated way that equipment triggers each other, the system has achieved efficient control of AUT beam controller and other instruments.

articleTitle: Study on characteristics of the ionospheric conductivity in the polar region
abstract: Based on the theory of ionospheric conductivity and the international reference ionosphere model (IRI-2007), the Pedersen and Hall conductivity change in different phases of the solar cycle during quiet geomagnetic activity was discussed. Meanwhile, because the International Reference Ionosphere model does not reflect the polar ionospheric conductivity very well during the geomagnetic storm. So applied the average energy and the energy flux of the precipitating electrons, the relation between the conductivity and the average energy and the energy flux of the precipitating particles under different energy spectrum function and the geomagnetic activity was analyzed. The results show that the variation of the ionosphric conductivity is good consistent with the change of the field-aligned currents in the polar region, and at the same time, it influenced by the solar activity and the geomagnetic substorm.

articleTitle: Analysis of GPS patch antenna covered by re-entry plasma sheath
abstract: A plasma sheath enveloping a reentry vehicle would affect on-board antennas performances greatly, especially the navigation antennas. This paper studies the effects of plasma sheath on a GPS microstrip patch antenna during a typical reentry phase. Utilizing the algorithm of time-domain finite integration, the radiation and admittance characteristics of the GPS antenna coated by plasma sheath are obtained. The changes in antenna characteristics are analyzed and the process of a reentry blackout is also reproduced from the respect of the antenna performance degradations.

articleTitle: An arbitrary high-order hexahedrons generation technology for DGTD algorithm
abstract: The Hexahedral Discontinuous Galerkin time domain (Hex-DGTD) algorithm required the computational domain divided into a set of nonoverlapping curved hexahedral subdomains. Each subdomain's Jacobian matrix must be obtained by mapping it into a standard cube. However, general commercial software can only divide computational domain into straight or low order hexahedral meshes, these meshes poorly conform to the geometry and bring in errors in DGTD boundary condition. This article proposed the technique of arbitrary high order curved hexahedral meshes combined with Gordon-Hall method, can conform to the geometry's boundary accurately, and reduce errors in getting each hexahedron's Jacobian matrix obviously. Numerical results verified the technique of generating curved hexahedral meshes improve the accuracy of the DGTD algorithm without increase computing resources significantly.

articleTitle: Analysis of ionospheric response to solar flares at Kunming site
abstract: We presented in this paper the ionosphere variation characteristics during solar flares with location, season and solar activity level at Kunming site (25.6°N, 103.8°E), using the data measured by MF radar and ionosonde. Results showed: (1) the maximum amplitudes both D region and f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">min</inf> during solar flares appeared near at noon; there was no the strict corresponding relationship during solar flares between F layer critical frequency (foF2) and location time. (2) seasonal variation of increasing amplitude of electron density in D layer during solar flares reached the maximum in summer; that of f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">min</inf> was maximal in autumn, second in spring; that of foF2 reached the maximum in winter, second in autumn and least in spring. (3) the variation of ionosphere showed the positive correlation with the level of solar flare. (4) the ionosphere of D region had different characteristics with F layer ionosphere during solar flare on November 4, 2008.

articleTitle: Research on Electrical Fast Transient/Burst immunity test technology for electricity meter
abstract: Aiming at the special problem of the Electrical Fast Transient/Burst (EFT/B) immunity test for electricity meter, design and development the corresponding power and pulse lines filters based on the simulation and analysis by using the EWB software, constructs the test system that can satisfy the requirements of electricity meter standard completely, also can always record the basic error values of electricity meter normally during the test process. The service condition indicated that this system is effective and accurate.

articleTitle: Digital active phased array antenna measurement method based on correlation technique
abstract: A new method which is to solve the problem of the digital active phased array antenna fast measurement method based on correlation technique is presented. In this method, a test probe is fixed in the mid-field of phased array antenna, for receiving orthogonal excitation signals sent by the elements; and the initial channel excitation can be fast restored by correlation detection; then with the active element patterns, the radiation characteristics of the array under test can be obtained. Finally, the simulation results of a digital active phased array antenna model are demonstrated here to illustrate the feasibility and accuracy of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Fast calculation of bistatic RCS for conducting objects using the adaptive cross approximation algorithm
abstract: Adaptive cross approximation (ACA) algorithm as a kind of common matrix compression method is often used to analyze the electromagnetic radiation and scattering problems. In the region of far field, the impedance matrix is compressed by ACA method, and the extracted impedance matrix is accelerated filling by equivalent dipole-moment method (EDM). In the area of near field, the method of moments or the equivalent dipole-moment method is applied for filling the impedance matrix. The iterative near field preconditioning technique is used to solve matrix equation, so that fast calculation of radar cross section (RCS) can be achieved. Numerical results show that the computational efficiency is improved significantly via applying the presented method in this paper without sacrificing much accuracy.

articleTitle: An improved time-frequency distribution method for ionosphere phase decontamination
abstract: Ionosphere phase contamination causes spectrum broadening of the OTHR ground Clutter and Sea Clutter, restricting the detection of slowly moving target on the sea seriously. In this article, a new method with high time-frequency cohesive and low cross item is put forward. The method is used to solve the problem of ionosphere phase contamination by Time-Frequency Distribution and it succeeded in solving the low time-frequency cohesive of STFT method and the high cross item of WVD method, improving the phase pollution suppression precision dramatically.

articleTitle: Observation debris RCS with the tristatic radar
abstract: We report results from the tristatic measurements of the space debris on May 25 2010, from 8UT to 23UT. A 15 hour measurement was run by using the 930MHZ(UHF) European Incoherent Scatter(EISCAT) radar system, which consist of three 32-meters antenna, recorded raw sample data used the standard EISACT receiver, and the transmission sample signal with Match Function(MF) analysis needed from simulation based on the constant experiment code. The resulting debris is clearly visible in the measurement, the detection threshold was set to ENR=40 in tristatic radar at the same time, and 14 events were obtained. The resulting debris are compared to a simulated observation produced with the debris orbit prediction model of National Astronomical Observatories, Chinese Academy of Sciences(CAS). The resulted showed that the absolute mean errors of 14 events in distance is 0.72km. The RCS measurements are found to have some extents with the debris value from U.S. Space Surveillance Network(SSN), although only a single measurement was made.

articleTitle: Fast range profile simulation using shooting and bouncing ray technique under arbitrary radar signal
abstract: The high resolution range profile (HRRP) is an important feature for automatic target recognition (ATR). However, it is very time-consuming to generate accurate range profiles of electrically large and complex targets. In this paper, we propose a fast range profile simulation approach that firstly calculates the scattering fields of targets with the shooting and bouncing ray (SBR) method, then assigns weights to fields of different frequencies according to specific radar signal and its match filter, and finally obtains the range profile by the inverse Fourier transform. Various examples involving canonical and complicated objects are presented to demonstrate the feasibility of the proposed method to accurately generate the radar range profiles.

articleTitle: The Time-Frequency Combination Measurement Method and its implementation for in-situ electronicmagnetic emission test
abstract: A Time-Frequency Combination Measurement Method is presented in this paper. The EMI signal is divided into two ways for signal processing in time and frequency domain respectively after analogue down conversion. The sampling and processing method in time domain is discussed. The function and the implementation of each module in measurement system are introduced. The in-situ test examples such as stationary EMI signal and non-stationary EMI signal are presented. The results show that the electronicmagnetic emission can be finished fast by time-frequency combination measurement, which has a good applicability.

articleTitle: The design of six-way S band power divider
abstract: A S-band planar six-way power divider which uses three compact, symmetric Wilkinson [1] dividers connected to a Luzzato [2] divider is proposed in this paper. Microstrips are used in the design of the six-way power divider over a frequency range of 3.1-3.4 GHz. The substrate of the six-way power divider has been manufactured in a hexagon structure. Good agreement has been obtained between the measured and simulated results.

articleTitle: A novel compact microstrip slot antenna with spirals
abstract: A novel compact slot patch antenna with two spirals on single thin substrate is introduced, which is 66% smaller than the conventional half-wave patch antenna. The four parallel slots on surface can enhance the length of current path and reduce the size of patch, the two spirals used can decrease the height of antenna at the same time. Good agreement between the theoretical and experimental results is obtained. The measured return loss curve and radiation patterns are all presented.

articleTitle: The ARIMA prediction model of rain-induced dynamic attenuation characteristics
abstract: In the paper, the ARIMA model is used for analyzing and forecasting the short-term dynamic characteristics of rain-induced attenuation. In this way, an ARIMA (Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average) model to forecast real-time dynamic rain-induced attenuation is established. The paper also analyses, evaluates and does the spectrum inspection to the model as well as the forecasting results.

articleTitle: The THz emission properties of GaAs photoconductive antenna with strong electric fields
abstract: The terahertz (THz) emission properties of GaAs photoconductive antennas with strong electric fields are discussed; the transient transport characteristics of non-equilibrium carriers (hot electrons) within the photoconductive antenna were comparatively analyzed. It is shown that there are significant differences in the average drift velocity variation with strong and weak electric field. In the initial phase, optical wave scattering is mainly caused by small-angle scattering, carriers are accelerated by ballistic transport to reach higher electron energy in a shorter time, and the transient drift-velocity quickly rises, which is a main reason of the stronger THz radiation.

articleTitle: Radiation characteristic analysis of ridged horn by aperture port excitation
abstract: In this paper, radiation pattern of ridged horn and array with aperture port excitation are calculated based on surface integral equation method. According to equivalent theory, field distribution of the EM wave propagating in ridged waveguide on cross section of which is transformed to equivalent electrical dipoles and magnetic dipoles, then radiating electrical field by these dipoles as excitation, induced current on wall of horn is solved by MoM. Total field by these equivalent dipoles and induced current form pattern of a ridged horn. Results are compared to finite element-boundary integral method such as FEM-MoM.

articleTitle: Coupling characteristics between leaky coaxial cables with and without obstacle
abstract: The coupling characteristics between two leaky coaxial cables (LCXs) with transverse slots are analyzed by employing an equivalent method and superposition principle. In the method, two cables are used as transceiver, and the coupling characteristics are studied by analyzing the received signals in two ports of the receiving cable when the structure parameters and frequency change. It is found that the received signals are the same as the transmitted signal, only with a time delay and attenuation in amplitude. When there is an obstacle between the cables, the received signals regularly change with the location of the obstacle. Based on the analysis, a location detection method which is valuable to the design of intrusion detection system is discussed.

articleTitle: Design of low noise and fast lock PLL by using switch matrix
abstract: A PLL frequency synthesizer is designed by using switch matrix and mixer, in order to reduce the phase noise and lock time. Using of bandwidth optimize, mixer, low noise VCO, and low noise crystal oscillator to optimize the system phase noise and also reduce the lock time. Switch matrix is used to reduce the spur and lock time. Test shows that the output phase noise is −151dBc@10kHz.

articleTitle: A series feed E-shaped microstrip antenna with high gain
abstract: A series feed E-shaped microstrip antenna is proposed in this paper with high gain. Double E-shaped elements with high gain are series-fed for gain enhancing, while elements space is adjusted for radiation efficiency enhancing. With optimized design of the proposed antenna, the measured bandwidth of VSWR<;1.5 is from 2.33~2.54GHz with the relative bandwith of 8.6%. At the covering frequency band of 2.4~2.5GHz for WLAN, the proposed antenna achieves the gain of larger than 12dBi with steady bandwidth of both E plane and H plane. As a series-fed array, the proposed antenna has the advantage of easy fabrication, but suffers from the beam direction offset with the frequency shifts at E-plane. With the optimal design, the beam direction offset angle controlled within ±1°.

articleTitle: A comparative study on the exit aperture in shooting and bouncing ray method
abstract: The shooting and bouncing ray (SBR) method is well known for providing more accurate results by including the scattering effect arising from multiple bounces. The fact that the fields tracking in the SBR method is calculated by only a geometrical optics (GO) approximation makes the choice of the exit aperture matter. In this paper, a comprehensive study is made on the exit aperture in the SBR method. Three kinds of exit aperture are compared, i.e., bounding box of the cavity, wavefront of the ray tube and the scatterer itself. Numerical simulations with the exit aperture of different kinds are conducted to verify the theoretical analysis and to draw some conclusions.

articleTitle: Full-controlled devices and SCR consisting of the mixed H bridge switch circuit
abstract: Usually the H bridge switch circuits of four power switches are all the full-controlled devices, where two of them are the low-end switched and two as the high-end switches. The low-end switch driver is simpler, and the high-end switch driver is relatively complicated. In this paper, a kind of use full-controlled devices and SCR consists of a mix of H bridge switch circuit was presented, in which, the low-end switches use full-controlled devices, high-end switches use SCR. Using SCR conductive self-locking characteristics, this H bridge switch circuit can make the high-end switch driver also became very simple, so simplify the H bridge driving circuit.

Author Keywords: H bridge switch circuit full-controlled devices

articleTitle: Design of a compact triple-band antenna for Bluetooth/WLAN/WiMAX applications
abstract: New design of a printed monopole antenna with two U-type slots for multi operating bands of wireless communication systems is presented. The proposed antenna, which occupies a small size of 30 ×30 ×1m m <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>, has triple-band (2.16-2.75 GHz, 3.51-3.8 GHz, and 5.0-6.5 GHz) for covering all the Bluetooth bands, WiMAX bands and WLAN bands. Details of the proposed antenna design are described and the effects of design parameters on antenna performance are investigated. This antenna configuration would be quite useful for wireless communication systems.

articleTitle: The effect of mutual coupling on the channel performance of MIMO communication system
abstract: The mutual coupling which has great effect on the performance of the multi-input multi-output communication system is particularly analysed. In this work, the mutual impedance of the dipole array is calculated and the effect of mutual coupling on the correlation and capacity of N×N MIMO system in i.i.d. channel is investigated. The results show that mutual coupling reduces the correlation between the antennas and the simulations show that mutual coupling results in degradation of the capacity of MIMO communication system.

articleTitle: An ununiform periodic slotted leaky coaxial cable used in the specific wireless communication system of subway
abstract: A new leaky coaxial cable (LCX) with ununiform periodic vertical slots is introduced in this paper. The related parameters are analyzed to design the LCX. Based on the application, the specific forms of LCX are introduced. By simulating with the HFSS software and testing under the related standards, the consistent results between the simulation and the measurement are obtained, both of which meet with the standards. The results indicate that the LCX has the advantages of low coupling loss, small transmission attenuation, low VSWR, and stable structure. It can be used in the specific wireless communication system of subway at the frequency of 800MHz.

articleTitle: Novel 3D RFID antenna with low profile and low cost
abstract: The RFID systems are used more and more widely, and the low profile and low cost antennas are strongly needed for some base stations. Here a novel 3D miniaturized RFID antenna is proposed. It consists of two vertical printed triangular monopole antenna elements. And top-loading is used to reduce the antenna's profile. Four tuning poles are adopted for better matching and broader bandwidth. The measured return loss is -33dB and its -10dB bandwidth is about 20%. The measured maximum gain is 3.73dB. Compared with conventional RFID antenna, 50% size reduction is achieved.

articleTitle: Scintillation of partially coherent Gaussian Schell-model beam propagation in slant atmospheric turbulence
abstract: Based on the modified Rytov theory and model of the ITU-R slant atmospheric structure constant, the uniform scintillation index considering inner- and outer-scales is derived from weak to strong turbulence regions with partially coherent Gaussian Schell-model (GSM) beam propagation in the slant path. The effects of the waist radius, wavelength of beams and inner- and outer-scales of the turbulence on scintillation are analyzed numerically. Results obtained show using the partially coherent beams instead of the fully coherent beams can reduce the scintillation effect in atmospheric turbulence. The study can be found wide application in atmospheric optical communication.

articleTitle: Numerical calculation on electromagnetic wave reflection by plasma-covered structures
abstract: We present real-time status of the electromagnetic (EM) scattering by the plasma-covered perfectly conducting structures, e.g., metal plate and metal cavity, using the two-dimensional finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) method. The absorption and refraction by plasma of such progresses are analyzed, in order to verify the feasibility and validity of the plasma stealth for cavity structure. The variations in their return loss as a function of electron density of plasma and plasma collision frequency are also presented. For plasma-covered metal cavity the return loss is found to be significant, even when it is slight for plasma-covered metal plate. The appropriate parameter regimes of plasma can be chosen for more efficiency design.

articleTitle: Application of iterative algorithm in target simulator channel calibration
abstract: The influence of channels' amplitude and phase errors on target position precision was simulated and analyzed based on the principle of binary array orientation. We calculated ratios of channels' electric field intensity corresponding to different target positions. An iterative algorithm which used in channel calibration of four-element-array target simulator is designed. Experimental results prove that it can satisfy the requirements of high accuracy, and is applicable to a lot of target simulation systems.

articleTitle: Generating plane waves in the near fields of pyramidal horn arrays
abstract: In the antenna far-field pattern testing and the RCS testing, the ideal incident field is a uniform plane wave. To approximate this condition, the pyramidal horn arrays have been simulated. The design procedure was based on a numerical near-field synthesis technique that produced a set of complex excitations for the array elements. The quasi uniform plane waves are obtained in the near fields of 4×4 and 6×6 pyramidal horn arrays. The calculation results of near fields are presented at 35GHz. The operating bandwidths of arrays are analyzed.

articleTitle: A novel method for analyzing electromagnetic scattering problems of space debris
abstract: Research on electromagnetic scattering characteristic of space debris is very important to detect and track orbital debris, which is helpful to use orbits effectively. The traditional algorithms of scattering computing are limited in computational efficiency. In this paper, we present Adaptively Modified Characteristic Basis Function Method (AMCBFM) for analyzing the EM scattering from space debris. Based on dividing the object structure into small blocks, the method can reduce the size of impedance matrix. Compared with Method of Moment (MM), this method reduces considerably the burden on the CPU time as well as memory requirements. We also provide a feasible ground simulation test method for EM scattering measurement of space debris. The result of measurement confirmed the accuracy and efficiency of the proposed method in speeding up solving large electrical scale problems. It can be used in EM scattering analysis of series of space debris.

articleTitle: The electromagnetic environment assessment of nuclear magnetic resonance device in hospital
abstract: The purpose of this paper is to assess electromagnetic environment of nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) device in hospital, in considering of the proposed construction of subway lines which would pass the hospital. A method is proposed to quantitatively analyze and evaluate electromagnetic interference of NMR device. It is derived through the analysis and evaluation: when subway line passes through the hospital, the field strength surrounding the hospital can reach 30dBuT to 40dBuT at several frequencies, which is greater than 20dBuT-the threshold of the NMR device. It can ensure the NMR equipment working normally, after applying an electromagnetic shielding measure which makes sure that the electromagnetic shielding effectiveness reaches 80dB.

articleTitle: A novel low profile box-shaped antenna for a repeater system
abstract: This paper presents a novel microstrip slot antenna based on box-shaped structure suited for a repeater system in the mobile communication cellular band (890MHz-960MHz). With the aid of folded-slot technique, the overall antenna size is only about 0.29λ × 0.29λ × 0.037λ (λ is the wavelength corresponding to the lowest edge of the operating band 860MHz). A 13.6% simulated impedance bandwidth, ranging from 865MHz to 990MHz, is obtained within 2:1 VSWR (Voltage Standing Wave Ratio). Furthermore, the prototype of the antenna is constructed and tested, and a 15% impedance bandwidth is observed. Experimental study is carried out by varying the height of the box. Simulated and measured results all show that this antenna exhibits wideband and low profile characteristics.

articleTitle: The fuze Doppler echo algorithm of near-field electromagnetic scattering model
abstract: A algorithm of fuze terminal trajectory Doppler echo signal is established based on the near-field electromagnetic scattering model and fuze echo model, which can calculating electromagnetic scattering characteristics of CAD model, and the fuze Doppler echo signal. Considering the questions of the shelter of the target and local irradiation, the algorithm mainly uses physical optics method(PO) and equivalent edge currents (EEC). Comparing with the measured data, the analysis shows that the example results using the algorithm mentioned above are, very consistent. The algorithm is reliable, and could provide the basis and approaches for proximity fuze design because of practicality and versatility.

articleTitle: A NTFF transformation method in planar near-field antenna measurement derived from FDTD
abstract: Focusing on the requirement of planar near-field antenna measurement, a method usually used in finite difference time domain simulation which is based on the equivalence theorem is employed in the process of near-to-far-field transformation. The distribution of the far-field pattern is obtained directly in polar spherical coordinate system. A standard gain horn antenna is taken as an example for testing. Near-field data, which are derived from theoretical formula and from numerical simulation, are transformed by this method. The results are compared with others obtained by traditional method based on plane wave spectrum expansion, analytical theory and electromagnetic computation with FDTD method.
